guides.title: Account and access
guides.summary: Accept invitations, complete MFA, confirm the current organization, understand roles, and resolve access problems.

sections.heading: Account and access
sections.text: Your Portal access is created through an organization invitation. The current organization and your role determine which Customer records and actions are available.

sections.heading: Accept an invitation
sections.text: Open the newest invitation link sent for your organization. Sign in with the same email address that received the invitation. Review the organization, your name, and the offered role. Accept or decline the invitation. An invitation link is private and can expire, be revoked, or be replaced by a newer link. Do not forward it. Phaeno tracks whether the invitation email was queued, delivered, bounced, or needs attention separately from whether the invitation is still pending or accepted. If an address hard-bounces, Phaeno must revoke the invitation and issue a new one to the corrected address. The portal does not collect or reset your sign-in password. Complete sign-in and account recovery through the identity service shown on the sign-in page.

sections.heading: Protect your account
sections.text: After your first sign-in step, connect an authenticator app and confirm the code it displays. Save the one-time backup codes shown during setup somewhere private and separate from the device running the authenticator. Never send an authenticator or backup code to Phaeno or your organization administrator. If you lose the authenticator but still have a backup code, use that code to sign in, then contact Phaeno to reset the authenticator enrollment. If you lose both the authenticator and every backup code, contact Phaeno directly. Phaeno will verify your identity and organization before resetting MFA; all active sessions are revoked and you must connect a new authenticator before Portal access resumes. Email can start the support request but does not itself bypass MFA.

sections.heading: Confirm the current organization
sections.text: The user menu shows the organization active in your current session. That organization scopes every portal read and action. Self-service switching between multiple external organization memberships is not currently available. If the wrong organization is shown, stop before opening a job or Data Library record and contact Phaeno. If an expected record or action is missing, confirm the current organization before reporting a problem.

sections.heading: Work within a department
sections.text: The header identifies your current organization and department. If you have access to more than one department, open the user menu and choose Department before opening or creating work. With a single available department, it is selected for you. Changing departments closes the previous workspace; finish or save your work before switching. Members see only their assigned departments. Organization administrators can select any active department in their organization, but the selected department still determines the records displayed. A department administrator's operational authority applies only to that department; it is not organization-wide access. Organization-wide data grants may be available in each department. If a department is unavailable or an expected Customer record is missing, ask your organization administrator or Phaeno to review the assignment. Do not change URLs to try to access another department. Organization and department administrators can open Departments from the user menu to manage the departments within their authority.

sections.heading: Manage department access and settings
sections.text: Organization administrators manage all departments, organization defaults, the default department, and department lifecycle. Department administrators manage settings and member access only in their assigned departments. A person can be an administrator in Research and a member in Operations; granting one department role does not grant organization-wide administrator rights. In Departments, use a department's actions menu to Edit settings or Manage members. To add an existing organization member, enter their exact email, choose Find member, and review the access change before confirming. Only an organization administrator can invite someone new through User management or change an organization role. Organization administrators already have access to every department and cannot be restricted by a department admin. An active member must retain at least one active department assignment. Organization administrators use Edit organization defaults to set the purchase-order rule, billing and notification email, and shipping and result instructions. A department override takes precedence; a blank override inherits the organization value, then the existing system or commercial fallback. Saved shipping and accepted-quote snapshots retain their recorded values. Result instructions do not change the storage destination or grant an ordering service. Invitations require reviewed department access for members. Select each department and grant its administrator role only when needed. Organization administrators receive access to every department, including future additions. If settings changed while you were editing, review your preserved entries against the latest version before saving again. Closing an unsaved form asks whether to discard the changes.

sections.heading: Understand roles
sections.text: Member can review the current Customer organization’s work and download files that have been released. Organization administrator can also create and submit laboratory requests, accept quotes, request cancellations, and manage organization membership. Department administrators have the applicable operational authority only within their assigned departments. Actions remain hidden or unavailable when the current organization or your role does not permit them. Phaeno can assist with access, but it cannot bypass the organization boundary to expose another Customer’s records.

sections.heading: Manage Customer members
sections.text: Customer organization administrators manage membership only for their current organization. In User management, active members and invited people appear in one list. A Pending invitation status means account registration is incomplete. Use the card’s actions menu to resend or revoke that invitation, edit an active member’s organization role, or deactivate another member’s membership. An administrator cannot deactivate their own membership from User management. Enter the person’s first name, last name, and exact sign-in email, but never copy or request an invitation token. A deactivated membership is restored only through a fresh invitation and acceptance. Contact Phaeno for a globally disabled account or an action the organization administrator cannot complete.

sections.heading: Resolve common access states
sections.text: | What you see | What to do | | --- | --- | | Invitation link unavailable | Ask an administrator to confirm the invitation access state and email-delivery state. Resend only a still-valid address; after a hard bounce, request revoke/reissue to the corrected address. Use only the newest link. | | Email does not match | Sign out and use the email address that received the invitation, or request a corrected invitation. | | No active memberships | Ask your Customer administrator to coordinate a fresh invitation with Phaeno. | | Wrong organization shown | Stop before opening records and contact Phaeno to verify the active membership. | | Organization unavailable | Ask Phaeno whether the organization is inactive. | | Account disabled | Contact Phaeno. A Customer administrator cannot override a globally disabled account. | | Authenticator lost, backup code available | Use one backup code to sign in, then contact Phaeno for an MFA reset. | | Authenticator and backup codes lost | Contact Phaeno for identity verification and an MFA reset. Do not send old codes. | | Expected action missing | Confirm the current organization, then ask an administrator to review your role. | Never send a password, sign-in code, invitation token, or browser storage value in a support message.

guides.title: Data Library and organization access
guides.summary: Use released lab-job data, assigned curated packages, and Customer organization access.

sections.heading: Data Library and organization access
sections.text: The Data Library provides a consistent place to review released lab-job data and Phaeno-curated data packages. The two sources remain distinct and retain their own release and access rules.

sections.heading: Open data for a lab job
sections.text: From a job under Lab services, open Data & results, then select Open in Data Library. The Data Library opens in that job’s context and shows only released result packages and files for the job. If nothing has been released, return to the job to review its processing, scientific-readiness, payment, or release status. Select View organization Data Library to leave the job context and return to the curated packages assigned to your organization.

sections.heading: Use the Data Library
sections.text: The organization Data Library shows active curated-package grants shared across your organization or assigned to your selected department. These packages are separate from laboratory job inputs and results. Each grant points to an exact, immutable package version. A later package publication does not silently change the version your organization received. You can review the package summary, scientific context, quality information, file manifest, and checksums. Active organization members can download individual files or a complete archive. The archive includes the manifest and every file in that version. Curated packages are read-only. Customer users cannot edit, republish, or grant them to another organization.

sections.heading: Understand access changes
sections.text: Phaeno may grant, upgrade, revoke, quarantine, or retire a package. Revocation or quarantine blocks new viewing and downloads but cannot recall copies already downloaded. If a prior download needs action, the portal gives organization administrators Customer-safe guidance. Organization and department administrators can review curated download history for the selected department. This includes downloads from packages shared across the organization. Organization administrators can switch departments to review each department's activity. Department administrators see only activity within their assigned departments. Older download records without a recorded department remain available only to organization administrators, for organization-wide grants or grants assigned to the selected department. Changing a person's department assignments does not move or erase their earlier download records.

sections.heading: Manage organization members
sections.text: The authorization model permits Customer organization administrators to invite members by email, choose member or administrator access, change eligible roles, and deactivate other users’ memberships only within their organization. An administrator cannot deactivate their own membership from User management. Invitations must be accepted by the invited email account. The User management screen saves invitations, eligible role changes, and membership deactivation to the Portal account system. Deactivation ends portal access without deleting the person or audit history, and restoring an inactive membership requires a fresh invitation. Phaeno administrators handle global account disablement and organization status. Every user should have their own account. Do not share sign-in credentials or use a shared mailbox as a substitute for an accountable user. Safety and withdrawal instructions about previously supplied data continue to go to current organization administrators during an organization suspension. These notices do not restore Portal access. Contact Phaeno if you cannot record a required response in the portal.

guides.title: Getting started
guides.summary: Confirm the current organization, understand access, and find Customer work.

sections.heading: Getting started
sections.text: Portal keeps your organization’s laboratory requests, sample progress, released results, commercial documents, curated data, and user access in one place.

sections.heading: Navigate the help center
sections.text: Guide navigation opens beneath the toolbar from the far-left edge of the screen. Its header identifies Documentation and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the tab. Choosing a guide closes an unpinned sidebar and displays the article.

sections.heading: Confirm the current organization
sections.text: The user menu shows the organization active in your current session. That organization controls which records and actions you can see. Customer information never carries across organizations. Self-service switching between multiple external organization memberships is not currently available. If the wrong organization is active, or your account belongs to more than one external organization, contact Phaeno before continuing.

sections.heading: Know your access level
sections.text: Customer organization administrators can create and submit laboratory service requests, accept quotes, request cancellations, and manage organization members. Other active members can review their organization’s jobs, follow progress, and download results that have been released. If an expected action is missing, first confirm the organization shown in the user menu. Your organization administrator can then check your membership.

sections.heading: Find your work
sections.text: Dashboard shows live organization-scoped counts and recent status for laboratory jobs and assigned data, with a User management starting point for administrators. Lab services contains each job from request and pricing through sample preparation, shipping, laboratory progress, and results. Data Library contains released data opened from a specific lab job and Phaeno-curated data packages explicitly assigned to your organization. For organization administrators, User management manages durable invitations, Member or Organization administrator roles, and membership deactivation. Docs opens these guides.

sections.heading: Keep submissions safe
sections.text: The initial laboratory request workflow is not a protected-health-information intake workflow. Do not enter patient names, dates of birth, medical record numbers, or other direct identifiers in request fields, notes, file names, or uploads. Use your organization’s own reference values and follow the instructions attached to the selected analysis.

sections.heading: Get help
sections.text: When contacting Phaeno, provide the portal request or sample reference and a description of the step you were performing. Do not send credentials, authentication tokens, or sensitive sample content in a support message.

sections.heading: Earlier Trial Projects
sections.text: If your organization converted from Prospect, Trial Projects retains the approved Trial history and available results in their original department. Conversion preserves existing download deadlines. See Trial history.

sections.heading: Search and browse guides
sections.text: Use Search documentation at the top of Docs to find a guide or a matching section. Results update after a short pause; use at least two characters. Try “sample shipping” or “results and billing”. Choose Filters to narrow results by Topic, Workflow, or Guide type. Clear filters removes those selections. Browse by topic opens guides for a topic without requiring search words. Workflow links and Related guides at the end of an article provide other ways to find relevant instructions. Select a result title to open its matching section. Your browser’s Back action restores the search and filters. Search uses the guides for your current organization; it does not include the public Website or operational records. A guide’s instructions do not change your account permissions. If no guides match, try fewer words or clear the filters. If search is temporarily unavailable, use Try again or Browse all guides. A documentation update may require Refresh page; guide browsing remains available while the update finishes.

guides.title: Request laboratory services
guides.summary: Price a Job from its sample profile, then enter or import, finalize, and ship its sample list.

sections.heading: Request laboratory services
sections.text: Customer organization administrators use Lab services to describe and price a Job before doing the detailed work of entering its sample list.

sections.heading: Review a Job initiated by Phaeno
sections.text: Phaeno may initiate a Customer-owned Job when your organization has already discussed the work with Phaeno. It appears in Lab services as Quote in preparation while Phaeno prices it. You do not need to submit that Job for pricing. Open the Job and review its committed sample count, biological-source composition, storage requirements, safety declaration, and notes. When Phaeno issues the quote and it becomes Quote issued, an organization administrator can review and accept it in Quote & billing. Phaeno cannot accept it for your organization. If the scope is incorrect, do not accept the quote; contact Phaeno so the Job can be returned for a corrected revision. Individual sample entry remains unavailable until your organization accepts the quote.

sections.heading: Create a draft
sections.text: Request lab service is available only while your organization has current ordering authorization and PSeq Lab Service is offered. If new Jobs are unavailable, the page explains whether Phaeno must enable ordering authorization or the service is temporarily unavailable. Existing accepted Jobs remain available and follow their normal hold or cancellation workflow. Open Lab services and select Request lab service. In Job pricing details, enter a unique Job name and each Biological source with its sample count. The Portal calculates the Job's total sample count from those source groups. Enter the Storage requirements and Safety declaration shared by every sample, and any optional Job notes. Do not enter a patient name or identifier. Select Create job. The portal assigns an immutable eight-character Job number using unambiguous uppercase letters and numbers. The new Job opens on its detail page. Individual sample entry remains unavailable until the price is issued and accepted. Other members can see organization work but cannot create, edit, submit, or commercially approve it unless they are an organization administrator. If an older draft still contains sample rows from the former workflow, the Job identifies them as legacy rows. Remove each row before submitting for pricing; enter the current sample roster again only after accepting the price.

sections.heading: Submit for review
sections.text: Complete the Job pricing details, then select Submit for pricing. Confirm that those details contain no patient identifiers, PHI, or unnecessary personal data. No individual sample list is required or permitted at this stage. Submission freezes the pricing profile revision. Phaeno can prepare pricing, request specific corrections, or reject work that cannot be performed. When corrections are requested, create and submit a new revision. The prior revision remains in the job history; it is not silently overwritten.

sections.heading: Review and accept a quote
sections.text: Laboratory services are priced per job. Phaeno issues an itemized, immutable POMS quote for the accepted scope. When your approved billing and tax information is available, the quote includes calculated tax and freezes those commercial terms. Otherwise the quote is labeled Pre-tax total, and applicable tax is calculated when the invoice is issued. A zero tax amount is valid for an exempt, non-taxable, or zero-rate determination. The quote is available after all non-billing readiness items are complete and a Customer administrator is active; billing must be complete before invoicing. Before accepting, confirm the committed sample count, biological-source composition, standard service scope, price, currency, expiration date, and whether the displayed amount includes tax or is pre-tax. Only a Customer organization administrator can accept the current unexpired quote. If the scope changes after acceptance, Phaeno issues a separate change quote. Added work does not begin until the applicable change is accepted.

sections.heading: Ship and track samples
sections.text: After accepting the quote, return to Samples & shipping. Add samples manually or download and complete the Job-specific CSV template. The CSV accepts exactly customer_sample_id, biological_source, and tube_count; it does not accept barcodes. Previewing a CSV does not change the Job. Confirming a valid preview atomically replaces the editable draft list. Do not ship physical samples before the quote is accepted and the exact roster is finalized. An early or unmatched package is quarantined and escalated by Phaeno; it is not accessioned or attached to active Job work. The final list must contain exactly the accepted number of unique non-PHI sample IDs, match every accepted source-group count, and give each sample a positive whole-number tube count. Finalize the list only after reviewing the no-PHI confirmation. Finalization authorizes the specimen-specific Lab work and lets Phaeno prepare the registered return kit. When the kit is fulfilled, match every physical Phaeno-supplied tube to the displayed tube slot. A sample with multiple tubes appears once per tube as Tube 1 of N, Tube 2 of N, and so on. Review the packet and record carrier details after the package leaves your organization. Shipping remains part of the Job. The Portal tracks receipt, accessioning, processing, external sequencing, data processing, scientific review, holds, and readiness for release. A job can remain in progress while different samples move through laboratory work. If Phaeno needs replacement material or clarification, the job shows a Customer-safe action and the current schedule health. Internal scientific investigation details are not shown. Ready for release means Phaeno's scientific review is complete and the final deliverable package is complete, checksummed, and malware-clean. It does not mean a file is downloadable until an authorized Result Release Manager publishes that sample. Invoice balance and credit status never gate PSeq result release.

sections.heading: Cancel work
sections.text: A draft can be discarded before submission. Before Phaeno accepts work, an administrator can cancel eligible scope. After acceptance, submit a cancellation request. Phaeno records whether the request is approved, partially approved, or declined. Any correction to an issued PSeq invoice is retained as an append-only credit, debit, or write-off adjustment rather than editing the invoice.

guides.title: Results and billing
guides.summary: Understand governed sample-level result release and POMS invoices, payments, and adjustments.

sections.heading: Results and billing
sections.text: Scientific readiness and Customer release are separate. The portal shows whether each sample is still being produced, scientifically approved, withdrawn, or available to download.

sections.heading: Follow sample progress
sections.text: Open a laboratory job to see each sample’s current state. Receipt, accessioning, laboratory work, data processing, result readiness, and completion are recorded independently so one delayed sample does not hide progress on the others.

sections.heading: Understand the release rule
sections.text: A PSeq result may be released after its final output package is complete, checksummed, malware-clean, and scientifically approved. An authorized Phaeno Result Release Manager publishes the selected sample; other samples can remain in progress. Payment balance, payment terms, tax state, and Customer credit do not gate release.

sections.heading: Download released results
sections.text: Open the laboratory job and select the sample. Confirm that the result package is marked available rather than still under review or withdrawn. Review the release details and download the available files. Each release is immutable and linked to its scientific approval, package version, checksums, and quality facts. A corrected result is delivered as a new version; it does not replace the audit history of an earlier release. Download and retention events are audited. If a file passes its retention cutoff, contact Phaeno for an authorized reissue. For a newly released result, the job's Data & results tab shows the retention schedule frozen at release. Standard deletion is the normal deletion time. Conditional grace through is used only when at least one file in that release remains undownloaded at the standard deadline; in that case the whole release receives the stated grace period. The displayed date and time include your browser's local time-zone label. Earlier releases created before retention snapshots were introduced do not show a schedule; contact Phaeno before relying on a deletion date for one of those releases. For governed PSeq packages, download status counts a file only after its complete response finishes successfully. A partial or interrupted transfer does not count. Completion must be saved successfully before the standard deadline to avoid grace. If availability changes while a download is being prepared, refresh the package before trying again. If the Portal cannot verify download timing, contact Phaeno; the dates already assigned to your package remain unchanged. One successful download by an authorized member satisfies that file for the organization. If any file was still undownloaded at the standard deadline, Grace period active keeps the whole package available through the final date. Completing the remaining files during grace does not shorten that period. Downloads closed removes new download access at the applicable deadline; it does not by itself mean that stored bytes have been deleted. Policy changes affect future releases and do not change dates already assigned to a package. A retention reminder, when enabled for the workflow, is addressed to active Organization admins and links to the normal Portal result page. The page shows current availability even if the email is older. Access withdrawal or deactivation can stop an in-progress transfer; restoring access requires a fresh download while the package is still available.

sections.heading: Use POMS invoices
sections.text: At job completion, POMS issues one numbered invoice. If the accepted quote included tax, the invoice preserves that frozen determination. If the quote was labeled Pre-tax total, POMS calculates applicable tax from the approved billing profile at invoicing. The invoice freezes its billing, tax, currency, and payment terms; its due date is the completion date plus those terms. The immutable invoice PDF is available to your organization. POMS does not collect payment-card information or provide online payment processing in this release. Receipts may be partially or fully applied to the invoice. Overpayments remain visible as unapplied cash until Finance explicitly allocates or resolves them. Corrections appear as retained credits, debits, or write-offs; an issued invoice is never silently rewritten.

sections.heading: Download other laboratory result releases
sections.text: Other managed laboratory files appear under their result release with the retention schedule assigned at release. Use Download package for its ZIP or Download for an individual file. Where retention enforcement is enabled, new file and ZIP requests close together at the applicable deadline. An incomplete release receives its stated grace period; completing it during grace does not shorten that period. The Portal refreshes availability after an unsuccessful attempt. Closed downloads do not mean bytes have been deleted. A file or package withdrawal, failed scan, or access removal can stop an active transfer. A failed ZIP does not count any file from that attempt; prior successful downloads remain counted. Earlier releases without a schedule keep their existing contract; contact Phaeno for guidance instead of inferring a date. Where scheduled retention notices are enabled for Lab releases, active Organization admins receive one download reminder if the release is incomplete at its warning checkpoint, and one grace notice if grace applies. A delayed reminder is skipped if every file has completed or the standard deadline has passed. There are no daily reminders. Notices contain the release reference, deadline, and a sign-in link to the laboratory job; open the job for current availability. Delivery problems do not extend retention dates. Contact Phaeno if a notice needs support.

sections.heading: Keep a release receipt
sections.text: Open View retained package receipt beside a release's retention schedule, then choose Print / save PDF. The receipt retains the complete file manifest, byte sizes, checksums, original deadlines, recorded completion and deletion facts, and any reissue links. It contains metadata, not copies of the scientific files. Times include your display time zone and their UTC value. For newly captured Lab releases, the receipt also retains the sample identifier, recorded supplier tube barcodes, and Phaeno accession as they stood at release. Historical releases may show that lineage was not recorded. Organization admins can also review the organization's downloader history; other members see the release facts available within their Department. A quarantined package cannot be downloaded. A preservation hold protects retained files without extending their download window. Contact Phaeno about either state. After deletion, an authorized reissue requires a newly prepared and approved package; the original receipt and dates remain unchanged.

guides.title: Prepare and ship samples
guides.summary: Match each Phaeno-supplied tube to a finalized sample tube slot, retain the crosswalk, and ship the package.

sections.heading: Prepare and ship samples
sections.text: For a normal Lab Service Job, sample entry begins only after the price is accepted and the compliant sample list is finalized. Promotional orders follow their approved allowance. Open the owning Job under Lab services, then open Samples & shipping to see the return kit, expected tube slots, destination, and packet status.

sections.heading: Keep your records connected to the tubes
sections.text: Each Phaeno-supplied tube has a permanent manufacturer barcode. Your organization administrator scans or enters that barcode beside the correct Customer sample and tube slot before anything is shipped. A sample may own more than one slot, shown as Tube 1 of N. Use a stable, non-PHI identifier that your organization can connect to its own sample record. Do not enter a patient name, medical-record number, date of birth, or other direct identifier. Phaeno preserves the tube-to-sample crosswalk in the Portal and in the shipment packet. Download the CSV or print the packet for your records. Your organization remains responsible for knowing what its Customer sample identifier means; Phaeno is responsible for retaining the identifier-to-tube association used for shipping and intake. If the wrong tube was assigned, an organization administrator can scan the replacement tube and record why the assignment changed. The earlier association remains in history. If a packet was already confirmed, saving the correction before shipment voids that packet and issues a corrected revision; destroy any unused copy of the old packet and print the replacement. Do not cover, alter, or remove the manufacturer barcode.

sections.heading: Confirm and ship
sections.text: Assign exactly one registered tube from the displayed return kit to every expected tube slot. Confirm the crosswalk only after checking every row. POMS then freezes the destination, instructions, manifest, packet barcode, and tube-to-sample crosswalk for that packet revision. Print the full packet. Follow the preparation and packing instructions, place the manifest inside the package, and use the ship-to page with the carrier label. The Phaeno packet barcode does not buy postage and is not a tube barcode. After handing the package to the carrier, record the carrier, tracking number, and shipment time on Samples & shipping in the job. If a tube cannot be matched confidently or its barcode will not scan, stop and contact Phaeno instead of guessing.

guides.title: Statuses and troubleshooting
guides.summary: Interpret job, sample, quote, payment, scan, and release states and resolve common problems.

sections.heading: Statuses and troubleshooting
sections.text: A laboratory job, each sample, its quote, and each result file have separate statuses. Read them together: a job may remain in progress while one sample’s result is ready or held for payment.

sections.heading: Laboratory job statuses
sections.text: | Status | Meaning and next action | | --- | --- | | Draft request | An administrator can continue editing or discard the request. | | Submitted for quote | Phaeno is reviewing the submitted revision. | | Changes requested | Open the request details, correct the identified items, and submit a new revision. | | Quote in preparation | Phaeno is preparing job-specific pricing. No approval is available yet. | | Quote issued | An administrator can review and accept the current unexpired quote. | | Placed, awaiting samples | The price was accepted. Enter and finalize the exact sample list; then follow the Job’s shipping instructions. | | In progress | Phaeno has begun the accepted work. Review individual sample statuses for detail. | | Results available | At least one result is ready. Its file may still be under a release or payment gate. | | On hold | Read the Customer-safe reason and complete the requested action or contact Phaeno. | | Cancellation requested | Phaeno is reviewing the request; work is not automatically cancelled. | | Completed | Accepted work and release handling are complete. | | Cancelled or declined | The job will not proceed. Review the history and any linked commercial adjustment. |

sections.heading: Sample statuses
sections.text: Expected, Received, and Accessioned track intake. Lab analysis and Data processing track active work. Data available means an output exists for that sample, while Completed means its processing is finished. On hold requires attention; Rejected means the submitted material cannot proceed under the current job. Sample release is independent. A clean result can be Ready, Payment hold, Released, or Withdrawn. Download is available only after release.

sections.heading: Quotes and payment holds
sections.text: Issued means the current quote is available for review. Superseded means a newer quote replaced it. Expired means its validity period ended; request a current quote. Accepted records agreement to the priced scope and opens sample-list entry. Laboratory work is authorized only after the exact compliant list is finalized. Credit-approved Customer organizations receive Net 30 release. Without approved credit, result download remains on payment hold. The current portal does not provide payment confirmation or a hosted payment page; contact Phaeno about the job rather than attempting to clear the hold in the portal.

sections.heading: Troubleshoot a missing result
sections.text: Confirm the correct organization and laboratory job. Check the individual sample status rather than only the overall job. Check whether the result is still being scanned, is on payment hold, or was withdrawn. If you believe the commercial requirement has been satisfied, contact Phaeno with the job number; the portal does not currently clear a payment hold from an accounting-system update. Modal action errors remain visible in the shaded header while you review the form. If the portal reports that the Job changed, it automatically loads the latest record and keeps your entered values. A pricing submission also clears its privacy confirmation so you can review the latest Job, confirm again, and resubmit safely. Rejected or failed file scans require Phaeno review; do not repeatedly upload the same file unless Phaeno asks you to. For support, provide the portal job and sample references, the visible status, and the time of the last action. Do not include credentials, tokens, patient identifiers, or sensitive sample content.

guides.title: Trial history
guides.summary: Find preserved Trial scope, results, and retention receipts after conversion.

sections.heading: Trial history after Customer conversion
sections.text: If your organization previously completed a Prospect Trial Project, Trial projects retains its approved scope, samples, customer-safe progress, results, and history in the original department. Active authorized members may view it. The same organization identity continues after Customer conversion. For Research Use Only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures. Trial result archives include a manifest identifying the approved scope and files. Do not enter or send PHI or sample identity mappings through this workflow. Conversion does not reopen a Trial or permit additional Trial submissions. Use the Customer laboratory-request workflow for new work. Trial results remain independent of Customer invoice, credit, or payment status. Use Retention and receipt to review the release's original file policy and download history. Conversion does not restart or extend warning, retention, or grace dates. After complete release, earlier partial archives direct you to the complete package. Download controls show progress and explain unavailable files, including closed retention access; the workspace refreshes after a transfer. Withdrawn, held, or deleted files remain unavailable; retained metadata is not a promise of byte restoration. Contact Phaeno with the Trial number if a reissue is needed.

guides.title: Account and access
guides.summary: Accept invitations, complete MFA, confirm the current Partner, understand roles, and resolve access problems.

sections.heading: Account and access
sections.text: Your Portal access is created through an invitation to a specific Partner organization. The current organization and your role determine which reagent, assembly, data, and administrative actions are available.

sections.heading: Accept an invitation
sections.text: Open the newest invitation link sent for your Partner organization. Sign in with the same email address that received the invitation. Review the organization, your name, and the offered role. Accept or decline the invitation. The invitation page shows the email address currently signed in. If it is not the invited email, choose Sign out and use invited email, then sign in with the correct account. The invitation remains available in that browser while you switch accounts, and the identity service returns you to the invitation page after sign-in or account creation. Invitation links are private. A link can expire, be revoked, or be replaced by a newer invitation. If it is unavailable, ask your Partner administrator or Phaeno to send a new invitation. The portal does not collect or reset your sign-in password. Use the account recovery offered by the identity service on the sign-in page.

sections.heading: Protect your account
sections.text: After your first sign-in step, connect an authenticator app and confirm the code it displays. Save the one-time backup codes shown during setup somewhere private and separate from the device running the authenticator. Never send an authenticator or backup code to Phaeno or your Partner administrator. If you lose the authenticator but still have a backup code, use that code to sign in, then contact Phaeno to reset the authenticator enrollment. If you lose both the authenticator and every backup code, contact Phaeno directly. Phaeno will verify your identity and Partner organization before resetting MFA; all active sessions are revoked and you must connect a new authenticator before Portal access resumes. Email can start the support request but does not itself bypass MFA.

sections.heading: Confirm the current Partner organization
sections.text: The user menu shows the organization active in your current session. That organization controls the offerings, negotiated prices, addresses, orders, assembly requests, data grants, and users you can see. Self-service switching between multiple external organization memberships is not currently available. If the wrong organization is shown, stop before opening or creating work and contact Phaeno. Information and commercial terms never carry from one Partner organization to another.

sections.heading: Work within a department
sections.text: The header identifies your current organization and department. If you have access to more than one department, open the user menu and choose Department before opening or creating work. With a single available department, it is selected for you. Changing departments closes the previous workspace; finish or save your work before switching. Members see only their assigned departments. Organization administrators can select any active department in their organization, but the selected department still determines the records displayed. A department administrator's operational authority applies only to that department; it is not organization-wide access. Organization-wide data grants may be available in each department. If a department is unavailable or an expected Partner record is missing, ask your organization administrator or Phaeno to review the assignment. Do not change URLs to try to access another department. Organization and department administrators can open Departments from the user menu to manage the departments within their authority.

sections.heading: Manage department access and settings
sections.text: Organization administrators manage all departments, organization defaults, the default department, and department lifecycle. Department administrators manage settings and member access only in their assigned departments. A person can be an administrator in Research and a member in Operations; granting one department role does not grant organization-wide administrator rights. In Departments, use a department's actions menu to Edit settings or Manage members. To add an existing organization member, enter their exact email, choose Find member, and review the access change before confirming. Only an organization administrator can invite someone new through User management or change an organization role. Organization administrators already have access to every department and cannot be restricted by a department admin. An active member must retain at least one active department assignment. Organization administrators use Edit organization defaults to set the purchase-order rule, billing and notification email, and shipping and result instructions. A department override takes precedence; a blank override inherits the organization value, then the existing system or commercial fallback. Saved shipping and accepted-quote snapshots retain their recorded values. Result instructions do not change the storage destination or grant an ordering service. Invitations require reviewed department access for members. Select each department and grant its administrator role only when needed. Organization administrators receive access to every department, including future additions. If settings changed while you were editing, review your preserved entries against the latest version before saving again. Closing an unsaved form asks whether to discard the changes.

sections.heading: Understand roles
sections.text: Member can review the current Partner’s work and download files that have been released. Organization administrator can also place reagent orders, submit assembly requests, accept quotes or eligible commercial changes, request cancellations, approve substitutions, and manage membership. Department administrators have the applicable operational authority only within their assigned departments.

sections.heading: Manage Partner members
sections.text: Partner organization administrators manage membership only for their current organization. In User management, active members and invited people appear in one list. A Pending invitation status means account registration is incomplete. Use the card’s actions menu to resend or revoke that invitation, edit an active member’s organization role, or deactivate another member’s membership. An administrator cannot deactivate their own membership from User management. Enter the person’s first name, last name, and exact sign-in email, but never copy or request an invitation token. A deactivated membership is restored only through a fresh invitation and acceptance. Contact Phaeno for a globally disabled account or an action the organization administrator cannot complete.

sections.heading: Resolve common access states
sections.text: | What you see | What to do | | --- | --- | | Access unavailable after sign-in | Choose Continue invitation if it is shown, then review and accept the saved invitation. Otherwise, sign out and reopen the newest invitation link. | | Invitation link unavailable | Ask an administrator to confirm it is pending and resend it. Use only the newest link. | | Email does not match | Sign in with the invited email or request a corrected invitation. | | No active memberships | Ask your Partner administrator to coordinate a fresh invitation with Phaeno. | | Wrong organization shown | Stop before opening records and contact Phaeno to verify the active membership. | | Organization unavailable | Ask Phaeno whether the organization is inactive. | | Account disabled | Contact Phaeno; a Partner administrator cannot override this state. | | Authenticator lost, backup code available | Use one backup code to sign in, then contact Phaeno for an MFA reset. | | Authenticator and backup codes lost | Contact Phaeno for identity verification and an MFA reset. Do not send old codes. | | Offering or action missing | Confirm the current organization, then ask an administrator to review your role or Phaeno to review Partner eligibility. | Never send a password, sign-in code, invitation token, or browser storage value in a support message.

guides.title: Data Library, billing, and organization access
guides.summary: Use curated data, understand commercial records, and manage Partner membership.
taskKeywords: Data Library, billing, and organization access

sections.heading: Data Library, billing, and organization access
sections.text: Partner access is divided among curated Phaeno data, operational Partner work, commercial records, and organization membership.

sections.heading: Use curated data
sections.text: The Data Library contains exact package versions that Phaeno explicitly granted across your Partner organization or to your selected department. Active members can review the package summary, quality information, manifest, and checksums, then download individual files or a complete archive. Packages are read-only and remain separate from reagent and data-assembly records. A later package version does not replace an existing grant automatically. Phaeno may revoke or quarantine access. Those actions block new portal viewing and downloads but cannot recall files already downloaded. Partner administrators receive safe follow-up guidance when action on prior downloads is required.

sections.heading: Understand commercial documents
sections.text: POMS preserves immutable quotes and commercial source records. Phaeno Finance prepares journal entries and invoices through a manual accounting handoff outside the Partner workspace. The portal does not collect payment-card information or provide hosted payment links. Reagent pricing is negotiated per Partner and snapshotted when an order is placed. Data-assembly pricing is per job through an immutable quote. Assembly credit status is a separate audited setting that determines Net 30 or paid-before-download release.

sections.heading: Manage the Partner team
sections.text: The authorization model permits Partner organization administrators to invite people by email and assign member or administrator access only within their organization. Invitations are organization-specific and must be accepted by the invited email account. The User management screen saves invitations, eligible role changes, and membership deactivation to the Portal account system. Membership deactivation preserves historical actions, and a fresh invitation is required for reactivation. Phaeno administrators control global account and organization status. Organization and department administrators can review curated download history for the selected department. This includes downloads from packages shared across the organization. Organization administrators can switch departments to review each department's activity. Department administrators see only activity within their assigned departments. Older download records without a recorded department remain available only to organization administrators, for organization-wide grants or grants assigned to the selected department. Changing a person's department assignments does not move or erase their earlier download records. Operational downloads and order exports remain scoped to the selected Partner and department, with the applicable release gate for downloads. Safety and withdrawal instructions about previously supplied data continue to go to current organization administrators during an organization suspension. These notices do not restore Portal access. Contact Phaeno if you cannot record a required response in the portal.

guides.title: Request data assembly
guides.summary: Submit inputs, accept a job quote, follow processing, and download outputs.

sections.heading: Request data assembly
sections.text: Partner organization administrators submit files and metadata under an active Phaeno assembly profile, receive a per-job quote, and retrieve outputs for delivery through their own customer relationships.

sections.heading: Create an input revision
sections.text: Open Data assembly and create a draft. Enter the Partner project or reference name. Choose an active assembly profile available to the selected Partner. Provide every required metadata value and data declaration. Upload allowed file types within the stated size limits. Files must complete the managed upload and clean-scan checks before submission. The current workflow does not authorize protected health information.

sections.heading: Submit and correct
sections.text: Submission freezes an immutable input revision. Phaeno may accept it for quoting, request field- or file-specific changes, or reject it with a Partner-visible reason. If changes are requested, create a corrected revision and resubmit. Earlier revisions remain preserved for traceability.

sections.heading: Accept the job quote
sections.text: Assembly work is priced per job. Phaeno issues an itemized POMS quote that becomes visible immediately after issuance. A Partner administrator accepts the current, unexpired quote and supplies the required purchase-order number. An accepted quote freezes the validated input, profile, and commercial snapshot. Later scope changes use a separate immutable change quote.

sections.heading: Track and download outputs
sections.text: The request shows intake review, queued work, processing, output review, output availability, holds, and completion. An approved output release contains an immutable manifest and one or more checksummed files tied to the source input revision and assembly profile. Credit-approved Partners use Net 30 and may download scientifically ready outputs after the commercial source record is created. Partners without approved assembly credit can see that outputs are ready but cannot download them; the current portal has no payment-confirmation action, so contact Phaeno about the request. Use Download package to retrieve every file in a release as one ZIP, or download a file individually. Only a complete server response counts. Partial, cancelled, failed, and timed-out transfers remain undownloaded, and an active transfer is shown as in progress until it reaches a terminal outcome. One completed download by any currently authorized Partner member satisfies that file for the organization; the Partner view does not expose the member's identity. Each newly released output shows the retention schedule frozen when that release became available. Standard deletion is the normal deletion time. Conditional grace through applies only when at least one file in the release remains undownloaded at the standard deadline; when that happens, the whole release receives the displayed grace period. Dates and times include the browser's local time-zone label. An earlier output created before retention snapshots were introduced does not show a schedule; contact Phaeno before relying on a deletion date for that release. A corrected output is a new release. Partner users download the release and deliver it through their own customer process; Portal does not collect the Partner’s end-customer identity or deliver directly to that customer. Before quote acceptance, an administrator may withdraw the request. After acceptance, use the cancellation-request workflow so completed work and financial history remain preserved. Where retention enforcement is enabled, file and ZIP requests close at the same frozen deadline. Grace period active keeps an incomplete release available through its stated final date; later completion does not shorten grace. A transfer admitted before cutoff may finish within its original time limit. File withdrawal, a failed scan, or removal of your access can stop an active ZIP. A failed ZIP counts none of its files from that attempt, while earlier successful downloads remain. Closed download controls do not indicate physical deletion. The page refreshes availability after an unsuccessful attempt. If timing cannot be verified, contact Phaeno; do not infer new dates for earlier releases without a schedule. These rules do not bypass payment holds or scientific release approval. Where scheduled retention notices are enabled for Assembly releases, active Organization admins receive one download reminder for an incomplete release and one grace notice if grace applies. A delayed reminder is skipped if every file has completed or the standard deadline has passed. There are no daily reminders. Notices identify the release and deadline and link to the authenticated assembly request; open it for current availability. Delivery problems do not extend the dates. Contact Phaeno if a notice needs support. Notices follow your Partner organization's admins and do not go to its end customers.

sections.heading: Keep an output receipt
sections.text: Open View retained package receipt beside an output's retention schedule and select Print / save PDF. The retained receipt lists every file, size, checksum, original deadline, recorded completion and deletion facts, and reissue links. It holds metadata, not downloadable copies. Times show the display time zone and UTC. Assembly outputs are identified as project-level files; the receipt does not infer sample mappings from the scientific manifest. Organization admins may review the organization's downloader history. Other members see authorized release facts within their Department. A quarantine stops downloads; a preservation hold does not extend the deadline. Contact Phaeno for support or an authorized reissue after deletion. Reissue requires a newly prepared, approved package and preserves the earlier receipt and dates.

guides.title: Getting started
guides.summary: Confirm the current Partner, understand access, and find Partner work.

sections.heading: Getting started
sections.text: Portal gives Partner organizations a tenant-isolated workspace for reagent orders, data-assembly requests, released outputs, curated data, and organization access.

sections.heading: Navigate the help center
sections.text: Guide navigation opens beneath the toolbar from the far-left edge of the screen. Its header identifies Documentation and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the tab. Choosing a guide closes an unpinned sidebar and displays the article.

sections.heading: Confirm the current Partner organization
sections.text: The user menu shows the organization active in your current session. Prices, offerings, requests, files, and permissions always come from that organization. A Partner cannot see another Partner’s negotiated prices or work. Self-service switching between multiple external organization memberships is not currently available. If the wrong organization is active, or your account belongs to more than one external organization, contact Phaeno before continuing.

sections.heading: Know your access level
sections.text: Partner organization administrators can create and place reagent orders, create and submit data-assembly requests, accept applicable commercial changes, decide substitutions, request cancellations, and manage members. Other active Partner members have read, progress-tracking, and eligible output-download access.

sections.heading: Find your work
sections.text: Dashboard shows live organization-scoped counts and recent status for reagent orders, data-assembly requests, and assigned data, with a User management starting point for administrators. Reagent orders contains the organization’s available products, drafts, placed orders, substitutions, and shipments. Data assembly contains input revisions, quotes, processing status, and released outputs. Data Library contains Phaeno-curated packages explicitly assigned to the Partner. For organization administrators, User management manages durable invitations, Member or Organization administrator roles, and membership deactivation. Docs opens the Partner guides.

sections.heading: Protect submitted data
sections.text: The initial workflows are not designed to collect protected health information. Do not place patient identifiers, credentials, or unnecessary confidential information in project names, notes, file names, manifests, or uploads. Use a Partner-controlled project reference and follow the metadata and file requirements shown by the selected assembly profile.

sections.heading: Get help
sections.text: Provide the portal order, request, shipment, or project reference when contacting Phaeno. Never include passwords, authentication tokens, or sensitive file contents in a support message.

sections.heading: Earlier Trial Projects
sections.text: If your organization converted from Prospect, Trial Projects retains the approved Trial history and available results in their original department. Conversion preserves existing download deadlines. See Trial history.

sections.heading: Search and browse guides
sections.text: Use Search documentation at the top of Docs to find a guide or a matching section. Results update after a short pause; use at least two characters. Try “reagent orders” or “data assembly”. Choose Filters to narrow results by Topic, Workflow, or Guide type. Clear filters removes those selections. Browse by topic opens guides for a topic without requiring search words. Workflow links and Related guides at the end of an article provide other ways to find relevant instructions. Select a result title to open its matching section. Your browser’s Back action restores the search and filters. Search uses the guides for your current organization; it does not include the public Website or operational records. A guide’s instructions do not change your account permissions. If no guides match, try fewer words or clear the filters. If search is temporarily unavailable, use Try again or Browse all guides. A documentation update may require Refresh page; guide browsing remains available while the update finishes.

guides.title: Order reagents
guides.summary: Use negotiated offerings, place orders, approve changes, and track shipments.

sections.heading: Order reagents
sections.text: Partner organization administrators order from offerings and negotiated prices configured specifically for their organization.

sections.heading: Prepare a draft
sections.text: Open Reagent orders and create a draft. Add only products offered to the selected Partner organization. Enter quantities that satisfy the offering’s minimum, maximum, and increment rules. Select an active shipping address from the Partner address book. Add any delivery note and the required purchase-order number. You can save and resume a draft or create a new draft from a prior order. The new draft uses current availability and pricing rather than copying stale commercial terms.

sections.heading: Place the order
sections.text: Placement revalidates the item, Partner eligibility, quantity, active negotiated price, shipping address, and purchase-order number. The portal then freezes the offering, price, currency, address, and PO snapshot. POMS preserves the actual negotiated price used for the order. Each shipment creates a journal-entry source record for Phaeno Finance; tax, freight, discounts, invoice preparation, and billing-address facts are handled outside the Partner workspace. Placement moves the local order directly into Phaeno review. It does not wait for an external accounting synchronization.

sections.heading: Review substitutions and changes
sections.text: Phaeno cannot fulfill a different reagent without explicit approval from a Partner organization administrator. A substitution request shows the original and proposed product and its commercial effect. Declining it preserves the original order facts. Any post-placement revision that increases the total requires Partner-administrator approval before Phaeno accepts it.

sections.heading: Track fulfillment
sections.text: Orders can be partially shipped. Each shipment can show carrier, service, tracking information, quantities, lot, expiration, and packing-slip details. The order keeps shipped and remaining quantities visible, including backordered units.

sections.heading: Cancel eligible work
sections.text: A draft or an unaccepted placed order can be cancelled. After Phaeno accepts the order, submit a cancellation request. Shipped quantities are never erased, and approved commercial changes remain in the order history and manual accounting source records.

guides.title: Statuses and troubleshooting
guides.summary: Interpret reagent, assembly, commercial, scan, shipment, and release states.

sections.heading: Statuses and troubleshooting
sections.text: Partner work has separate operational, commercial, file-scan, and release statuses. A completed workflow does not by itself mean every file is downloadable.

sections.heading: Reagent order statuses
sections.text: | Status | Meaning and next action | | --- | --- | | Draft | An administrator can continue editing or discard the order. | | Placed or under review | Phaeno is validating the frozen order and commercial terms. | | Accepted or processing | Phaeno accepted the order and fulfillment is underway. | | Partially shipped | Review shipments and the quantities still open or backordered. | | Shipped | All current quantities have shipment records; use the tracking details shown. | | On hold | Read the Partner-safe reason and complete the requested action. | | Cancellation requested | Phaeno is reviewing the request; shipped work is not erased. | | Fulfilled | Fulfillment is complete. | | Cancelled or rejected | The order will not proceed. Review the history and any commercial adjustment. | A proposed substitution is a separate decision. A Partner administrator must approve it before Phaeno can replace the ordered reagent. A declined substitution preserves the original order facts.

sections.heading: Assembly request statuses
sections.text: Draft is editable. Submitted and Intake validation mean Phaeno is checking the frozen input revision. Changes requested requires a corrected revision. Quote in preparation and Quote issued cover job-specific pricing. After quote acceptance, Placed/queued, Processing, and Output review track work. Output available means an output exists but it may still have a release or payment gate. On hold, Cancellation requested, Completed, Cancelled, and Rejected describe the remaining outcomes.

sections.heading: Commercial and file states
sections.text: Superseded or Expired quotes cannot be accepted; review the current quote or request a new one. Credit-approved Partner assembly work uses Net 30 release. Otherwise output remains on Payment hold; the current portal does not provide payment confirmation, so contact Phaeno about the request. Assembly inputs and outputs must complete validation and a clean scan. Rejected, Failed, or Unavailable scan states require Phaeno attention. A file is downloadable only when its release status is Released. Ready does not bypass a payment gate, and Withdrawn files remain unavailable. Reagent orders use the negotiated price captured at placement. Assembly work uses an accepted per-job quote. Phaeno Finance uses manual accounting source records outside the Partner workspace to prepare invoices and journal entries; the portal does not collect payment-card information.

sections.heading: Troubleshoot common problems
sections.text: Cannot place a reagent order: confirm the Partner organization, administrator role, active offering, quantity rules, shipping address, and purchase-order number. Cannot accept a quote: confirm it is the current issued, unexpired quote and that you are a Partner administrator. Upload rejected: compare the file name, type, size, and metadata with the assembly profile. Do not repeatedly upload a file rejected by scanning. Output missing: check output review, scan, release, and payment states separately. Order changed while open: refresh and review the latest version before attempting the action again. Shipment incomplete: review shipped and remaining quantities; a partial shipment can leave backordered units open. For support, provide the portal order or assembly reference, visible status, and last-action time. Do not send credentials, tokens, confidential data files, or customer information in a support message.

guides.title: Trial history
guides.summary: Find preserved Trial scope, results, and retention receipts after conversion.

sections.heading: Trial history after Partner conversion
sections.text: If your organization previously had a Prospect Trial Project, Trial projects preserves the approved scope, samples, customer-safe progress, releases, and history in the original department. Active authorized members may view that history under the same organization identity. For Research Use Only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures. Keep PHI and sample identity mappings outside the Portal. A Trial release archive includes its approved scope/file manifest. Partner conversion does not reopen a Trial or authorize new Trial samples. Partner reagent orders and data-assembly requests use their own workflows and permissions. Trial results are not subject to Partner pricing or payment gates. Open Retention and receipt for the original release policy and download history. Conversion does not extend file retention or grace dates. After complete release, earlier partial archives direct you to the complete package. Download controls show progress and explain unavailable files, including closed retention access; the workspace refreshes after a transfer. Download available files before the displayed deadline. Withdrawn, held, or deleted files remain unavailable; retained history does not restore deleted bytes. Contact Phaeno with the Trial number if a reissue is needed.

guides.title: Configuration and accounting recovery
guides.summary: Maintain scientific, commercial, accounting, credit, and sample-shipping rules.

sections.heading: Configuration and accounting recovery
sections.text: Order configuration controls the active scientific, Partner, commercial, release, and integration rules used by new work. Changes must be audited and should not rewrite immutable order snapshots. File management separately controls the retention policy used by future released result and output packages. Only a Phaeno platform administrator can change these settings. Use the far-left Order configuration sidebar to move among Defaults, Catalog, Analyses, Sample shipping, PSeq kits, Assembly, and Credit. On wider screens the sidebar can remain pinned; when it is unpinned or the screen is narrow, open the same non-modal navigation from the edge tab. The selected subject appears in the main pane without duplicating the navigation above the configuration form.

sections.heading: Maintain commercial configuration
sections.text: Maintain active billable items under Catalog, including a permanent item code, name, description, sales unit, base price, currency, and availability. Link these Phaeno-owned items to portal analyses, Partner reagent offerings, or assembly profiles. The designated laboratory-service item must use the permanent code pseq-lab-service, the sales unit specimen, and an active state. The catalog identifies it as PSeq Lab Service. POMS blocks laboratory quote issuance when this exact item is missing, inactive, or uses another unit; an unrelated specimen fee cannot replace it. Configure Partner reagent availability, negotiated price, currency, effective period, quantity rules, and shipping restrictions for each eligible Partner. Overlapping active price periods for the same Partner and item are not allowed. Configure Customer laboratory and Partner assembly credit separately. Approval means Net 30 release under the applicable workflow. Without credit, ready files remain on payment hold. Manual payment confirmation and release are not part of the current workflow; do not bypass that hold with an order-status change. Set the default quote-validity period in configuration. The initial default is 30 days, and an issued quote snapshots its own expiration.

sections.heading: Maintain scientific configuration
sections.text: Analysis definitions describe required Customer sample fields, instructions, expected outputs, and linked quoteable items. Assembly profiles describe Partner metadata, allowed files, validation, expected output contract, availability, and linked quoteable items. Deactivate configuration that must not be used for new work. Existing orders keep their accepted definitions, profile versions, prices, currency, and commercial snapshots.

sections.heading: Maintain sample-shipping configuration
sections.text: Use Sample shipping to maintain three controlled record sets: ship-to destinations with the full address, receiving team, receiving hours and time zone, closure guidance, delivery directions, and carrier restrictions; sample types with material, quantity, primary-container, temperature, packaging, customer-label, prohibited-identifier, safety, and transit requirements; and one instruction rule for an exact destination revision and sample-type revision, including compatibility grouping, packing, carrier, dispatch, delivery, required-document, exception, and optional customs instructions. New records default to inactive. Activate a revision only after the address and scientific and operational instructions are approved. Selecting Create revision copies the current content into a new record and ends the prior revision when the new revision becomes effective; it does not rewrite history or any packet snapshot already issued. Use Instruction preview before operational use. Select an exact destination revision, one or more sample-type revisions, and the time to evaluate. POMS displays the full resolved ship-to and detailed preparation instructions. If a required combination rule is missing, compatibility groups differ, or a type requires its own package, POMS blocks a combined preview so the work can be corrected or split. This configuration is shared infrastructure only. It does not create a Prospect Trial Project, grant a Customer promotion, place an order, or activate any real destination or sample type on its own. Return-kit fulfillment is operated from Order intake, not from configuration. The fulfillment record preserves shipper product/lot facts, the exact registered supplier-tube inventory, and outbound tracking. The current Corning vial and Therapak shipper values are pilot candidates only; activate real work only after representative tubes, shipper fit, returned volume, seal, freezing, dry-ice handling, barcode scanning, and degraded-mode procedures pass the physical validation gate.

sections.heading: Maintain released-deliverable retention
sections.text: Open File management to review or edit the global released-deliverable policy. The starting values are 30 days of standard retention, one undownloaded-package warning 5 days before the standard deadline, and a conditional 5-day grace period when any released file remains undownloaded at that deadline. Every value is a positive whole number of exact 24-hour days, and the warning lead must be shorter than standard retention. Enter a reason for every change. A new revision applies only to packages released afterward; it never changes a deadline already communicated for an existing release. Prior revisions remain visible in policy history. To configure a Company-specific policy, open the Customer, Partner, or Prospect in CRM Companies, find Portal access and services, select Retention, and add an override. Leave any value blank to inherit that value from the current global policy. The page shows the effective value and source for each field. Removing an override restores global inheritance for future releases and also requires a reason. New Customer laboratory-result and Partner data-assembly output releases now freeze the effective policy version and exact UTC warning, standard-deletion, and potential final-deletion times in the same transaction as release. Their authorized external detail views show the standard deadline and label the later date as conditional until grace is actually activated. Repeated payment events preserve the first release time. Releases created before the snapshot migration are not backfilled and show no automated retention schedule. Released-file and full-package ZIP downloads now create a bounded, immutable transfer attempt before storage opens. The attempt counts only after the complete server response succeeds. Partial range responses, failures, cancellations, and timeouts do not count. Abandoned started attempts are reconciled after their frozen lease expires. Existing audit rows from before completion-aware tracking are retained as non-counting legacy_completion_unverified failures rather than being reclassified as successful downloads. Governed PSeq packages now use this same frozen policy and completion-aware grace/cutoff evaluation. Their download requests obey the applicable deadline independently of cleanup. Existing PSeq schedules retain their original dates. Automatic warning/grace notices, durable checkpoint processing, general release enforcement, and package-byte deletion remain separate activation work. A closed download window does not prove that bytes were deleted.

sections.heading: Prepare manual journal entries
sections.text: Open Order operations, then Accounting, to review the Journal-entry source report. Choose an inclusive UTC accounting-date range and download the CSV for manual entry into the accounting system. POMS creates one stable source record when a laboratory job reaches its billing boundary, an assembly output is approved, or a reagent shipment is recorded. The report provides the stable entry ID, organization, workflow and source references, purchase-order or project reference, currency, gross amount, outstanding balance, payment status, and memo. Finance assigns general-ledger accounts, tax treatment, and posting dates outside POMS. Repeated downloads do not mark a row as posted. QuickBooks Online integration is deferred. Do not configure OAuth, retry historical QuickBooks messages, or treat a report download as payment confirmation.

sections.heading: Activate production dependencies
sections.text: Before production use, confirm approved storage and malware scanning, notification delivery, active catalog and scientific profiles, Partner offerings and prices, credit decisions, quote validity, the manual accounting handoff, and operational ownership. Laboratory activation also requires approved bench workflows, label/printer/scanner and degraded-mode procedures, external NGS provider operating details, and the required database-backed verification. A successful application build alone does not prove these production dependencies are ready.

sections.heading: Recover a retention notice
sections.text: Filter Owned attention queues to Retention notices. An urgent item identifies the package, deadline, and notification requiring recovery. Confirm active Organization administrators, correct the delivery issue, and retry the existing notification. A later grace notice uses the original final date. Resolution does not extend retention or confirm physical deletion; a persisting delivery failure can reopen the item.

sections.heading: Preserve a release or record a reissue
sections.text: A Phaeno platform administrator can open File management → Released packages, find the organization, and open a package's retained receipt. The detail page shows its full manifest, checksums, original retention dates, download evidence, cleanup outcome and reissue history. Use Print / save PDF for a metadata copy. A historical release may lack captured sample lineage; do not infer missing facts. Choose Place hold, select the hold type, and record the reason. Preserve bytes blocks physical cleanup. Quarantine and suspend access also stops current transfers and blocks new downloads; it is available only where download monitoring is active. Neither action resets retention. Hold reasons remain in the Phaeno management view rather than the external receipt. Use Release hold with a reason when preservation is no longer needed. If the original deadline has passed, cleanup may proceed once every hold is released and active transfer leases have ended. A stale-record error refreshes the details and preserves your entered reason; review the current state before retrying. After deletion, first regenerate and approve a new package through the owning scientific workflow. Then open the old receipt and choose Link reissued package, select the eligible new release, and record the authorization reason. POMS requires the same organization, workflow and sample where applicable, new file objects, and a release created after the original deletion. Linking never restores deleted bytes or changes the original release dates. Cleanup can remain pending for active transfers, preservation, shared source files, an incomplete package, or provider failure. Provider failures are retried against the same objects. Files deleted records successful physical cleanup; Downloads closed alone does not. Escalate repeated failures with the package reference and safe status, without copying credentials or scientific files.

guides.title: Customer relationship management
