When an incoming package includes a Phaeno shipment packet, open Lab operations > Receipt & accession and scan the packet and each registered supplier tube first. That comparison identifies the exact expected sample and linked Lab work but does not record receipt. The packet barcode is not a specimen or container barcode and must not be copied into an accession or container field.

sections.heading: Accession the specimen
sections.text: Accession only after receipt. Choose a unique accession number, then record location, quantity and unit when tracked, and an optional retention date. For a shipment with a frozen registered-tube crosswalk, scan both the packet and each matched tube during accession. POMS validates the exact shipment, specimen, and tube-slot association and adopts every qualified permanent supplier barcode as a submitted-container identity. Multiple submitted tubes for one sample use the same specimen accession and create separate containers linked to that specimen. POMS does not create or print a second label for those tubes. For every other submitted specimen, POMS assigns its own authoritative barcode as before. The label window renders the current container identity as a Code 39 barcode through the browser and installed printer driver. Enter the reason, open the system print dialog, and inspect the physical label before choosing Label printed. POMS increments the print count only after that confirmation. If the label did not print correctly, enter the failure details and choose Record failed attempt; the failure remains in history without falsely counting a usable label. Every POMS-generated label reprint requires a reason and renders the same current container identity. A reprint or failed attempt adds a separate history event; it does not replace the barcode or erase an earlier print. Registered supplier tubes have no POMS print action. Verify readable text, barcode, accession, container, and adhesion using the approved bench procedure before processing continues.

sections.heading: Scan and locate a container
sections.text: Use Work > Scan a container to find the exact work order, accession, container status, location, parent barcode, and associated library. Place the cursor in the container-barcode field and scan either an adopted registered supplier barcode or a POMS-generated barcode. Code 39 start and stop characters and letter case are normalized; an altered checksum, incomplete barcode, or unknown barcode is rejected without opening another record. The field returns focus after the result so repeated scans remain efficient.

sections.heading: Preserve physical lineage
sections.text: Create child containers for aliquots, prepared reagents, libraries, or other derived materials. Select the immediate parent container and record the quantity and unit required by the approved procedure. POMS assigns each child container its own barcode and opens its label window after creation. The lineage must allow an operator to scan a derived container and trace it through its immediate parent to the submitted specimen. Do not reuse a barcode, move material by editing its parent, or delete a container to repair history. Record the supported correction or new derived container.

sections.heading: Apply the intake decision
sections.text: After accession, record Accepted, On hold, or Rejected. Holds and rejections require an approved reason code and a safe explanation when Customer action is required. When every expected specimen has an intake decision, the work order reaches Received.

guides.title: Scientific approval and release readiness
guides.summary: Review complete lineage and clean final artifacts, enforce actor separation, and pin the approved package.

sections.heading: Scientific approval and release readiness
sections.text: Scientific approval is the final Lab Ops decision. It confirms that the authorized laboratory work satisfied the configured execution and exception gates. It is not a Customer file publication action.

sections.heading: Enter scientific review
sections.text: Move work into Scientific review only after required receipt, accession, executions, QC, libraries, batches, and sendout facts are complete for the approved release scope. Confirm that every assigned execution is completed or explicitly abandoned, every blocking exception is resolved, and the registered final-result package has every expected checksummed, malware-clean artifact. The Scientific Reviewer should be able to trace the submitted specimen through containers, material lots, equipment, protocol versions, captured results, library preparation, batches, and provider custody as applicable.

sections.heading: Record the approval
sections.text: Record the release-definition key and version, reviewer identity, approval time, permitted QC projection, and exact output-package identifier/version. Approval pins that immutable package; it does not upload or alter artifacts. The reviewer must be different from every actor who recorded receipt, accessioning, execution, QC, library, batch, or sendout work in scope. A protocol author cannot approve or activate that protocol version. If either actor-separation or scientific gates fail, leave the work in review and create the appropriate exception or rework action.

sections.heading: Publish readiness
sections.text: Approval moves the Lab work order to Ready for release and publishes the controlled Customer-safe milestone to Commercial. Commercial may receive the milestone, schedule health, expected timing, and safe QC projection defined by the contract.

sections.heading: Respect the release boundary
sections.text: Ready for release automatically creates the Commercial release candidate for the approved package. It does not publish the result. A Result Release Manager still controls Customer visibility, and payment/credit facts never gate PSeq release. If the Lab-to-Commercial event fails, retry the existing durable projection. Do not duplicate the approval, recreate the work order, or manually mark the Customer file released.

guides.title: PSeq billing, cash, and result release
guides.summary: Operate POMS invoices, receipts, allocation, reconciliation, and scientifically governed PSeq release.
taskKeywords: PSeq billing, cash, and result release

sections.heading: PSeq billing, cash, and result release
sections.text: POMS owns operational accounts receivable for PSeq Lab Service. Result release is scientifically governed and never gated by payment balance or credit. Partner PSeq Kit and Partner data-assembly payment/release rules remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Configure and issue PSeq documents
sections.text: Record billing contact/address and Net 30 terms by default. Record Taxable, Exempt, or NonTaxable, including the approved rate or exemption evidence. Finance approval is required before the tax determination can be used. If the profile is complete and approved at quote issuance, POMS includes calculated tax and freezes billing, tax, terms, currency, and configuration version in the quote. Zero calculated tax is valid. If the profile is not ready, issue an explicitly pre-tax quote. Complete and approve the profile before invoicing; POMS then calculates tax and freezes the current billing terms in the invoice. Job completion idempotently creates one numbered invoice and immutable PDF. Due date is completion plus the applicable snapshotted terms. POMS calculates the approved tax rate without a tax engine. Never edit an issued invoice; use an append-only credit, debit, or write-off adjustment.

sections.heading: Release PSeq results
sections.text: A Customer result may be published only when the specific sample package is complete, checksummed, malware-clean, and scientifically approved. The Result Release Manager releases or withdraws a version. Other samples may remain in progress. Do not consult invoice balance or credit status for this decision. Corrections create a new package, scientific approval, and release version. Preserve notification, Customer download, retention warning/cutoff/grace/deletion, withdrawal, and authorized reissue evidence.

sections.heading: Review governed result retention
sections.text: New PSeq releases use the effective versioned policy from File management, including an active Organization override. The package and laboratory release share the same first release instant and freeze their policy and deadlines together. Existing schedules keep their original dates; do not change them by editing current configuration. The Customer package shows full-response download completion and the frozen standard/final dates. Grace remains usable when any artifact was undownloaded at the standard deadline; later completion does not shorten grace. New download requests close at the applicable deadline even if cleanup has not run. A request-only historical download event is not completion evidence. Success saved after the standard deadline cannot cancel grace. If download timing cannot be verified, ask technical support to recover the retained timing evidence; do not recreate the release or change its dates. This timing-recovery error is separate from the Retention notices queue. Where governed retention processing is enabled, POMS queues one warning for an incomplete package and one grace notice if grace applies. A delayed warning is skipped once all files have completed or the standard deadline has passed. Queued notices use current active Organization admins; they contain the package reference, deadline, and an authenticated Portal link. Use Owned attention queues → Retention notices to find urgent missing-recipient or delivery failures. Review the organization and administrator access, correct delivery configuration when needed, then retry the existing record in the notification workspace. Recreating a release or notification is not a recovery step. A failure can reopen the Operations item until the underlying notice is recovered. Deadlines remain unchanged. Physical cleanup remains separately controlled. A closed download window is not proof of byte deletion, and a queued message is not proof of receipt. Access withdrawal or deactivation stops a governed transfer; restoring access does not resume that transfer.

sections.heading: Record and reconcile cash
sections.text: Manual receipt entry requires payer, amount, USD currency, received date, method, bank reference, evidence, and external ID. CSV intake is preview-only until explicit confirmation and must include source, external ID, date, amount, currency, payer, reference, and memo. Matching suggestions never apply cash. Allocate explicitly so partial, one-receipt/many-invoice, many-receipt/one-invoice, overpayment, and unapplied cash remain visible. Reversals retain actor and reason. A Cash Operator submits a balanced reconciliation; a different Cash Reconciler who contributed none of its activity approves the immutable closeout report.

sections.heading: Apply Partner assembly release gates
sections.text: An approved output release must reference the accepted input revision and active assembly profile. Its accounting source record is created at output approval. A Partner with approved assembly credit may receive the output under its terms; otherwise the files remain on payment hold until a separately approved payment-confirmation workflow exists.

sections.heading: Diagnose a blocked release
sections.text: Review package completeness, checksum/scan state, scientific approval, release decision, notification, and retention independently from invoice/receipt/allocation/reconciliation. Never bypass a failed package gate by attaching a file manually or changing an unrelated workflow status. Use the owned attention queues for overdue invoices, unapplied cash, and reconciliation differences.

sections.heading: Support general Lab and Assembly downloads
sections.text: Where general retention enforcement is enabled, individual files and whole ZIPs use the release's frozen policy and verified completion. A closed window prevents new requests, while an admitted transfer can finish within its time limit. Current file withdrawal, scan failure, Organization/Department access removal, or release withdrawal stops active downloads. A failed ZIP does not count its files from that attempt. Partner payment-release rules still apply. Recover missing timing evidence through technical support without recreating the release or changing dates. General download enforcement does not itself schedule warning/grace emails or activate storage cleanup. Preserve the original contract for undated historical releases. Where general Lab/Assembly retention processing is enabled, the same warning, grace, and Retention notices recovery workflow applies to those releases. The Lab notice opens the laboratory job; the Assembly notice opens its assembly request. Recipients are current active Organization admins, including admins appointed after the notice was queued. Department-only members and notification routing aliases are not recipients. Retry the existing failed notification after correcting the cause, then review the Operations item. Preserve the original release and dates. General and governed PSeq notice processing are activated separately; a disabled process does not create or dispatch its scheduled notices. Released package schedules link to retained receipts. Receipts preserve file manifests, checksums, deadline/completion/deletion facts and reissue lineage after byte deletion. For preservation, quarantine, or linking a newly approved reissue, use Configuration and recovery.

guides.title: Customer lab authorization
guides.summary: Review Job pricing profiles, issue POMS quotes, and authorize Lab work after roster finalization.

sections.heading: Customer lab authorization
sections.text: Customer laboratory work enters Order Ops as a Commercial request. Order Ops validates the Job-level specimen count, biological-source composition, storage, safety, and service profile before pricing. Individual samples do not exist yet.

sections.heading: Initiate an order for a Customer
sections.text: An authorized Phaeno order-pricing user can begin the pricing profile when the Customer is already known and does not need to create the request first. Open Order operations, select Order intake, and choose New Customer order. Wait for the eligible Customer list to load, search incrementally by Company name, then select the Customer from the matching results. New Customer order remains unavailable while the list is loading or could not be loaded. Names come from canonical active CRM Companies. A Company appears when its attached active Customer operational scope is not manually blocked and has a current Ready PSeq Lab Service entitlement plus the active canonical specimen offering. It does not need an online administrator at this stage. Enter a unique Job name, every biological source and sample count, the shared storage requirements and safety declaration, and any Customer-safe Job notes. If Sales discussed a price, select Propose a price, enter the proposed USD price per specimen, and optionally add Customer-safe pricing context. A proposal is not a quote and does not authorize work. Do not enter individual sample IDs, tube barcodes, patient identifiers, or PHI. Confirm that the pricing details contain no patient identifiers, PHI, or unnecessary personal data, then select Start pricing. POMS creates the Customer-owned Job with one immutable submitted request revision and opens it in Quote in preparation. Review the committed sample count, source composition, storage, and safety facts on the operational detail. If a price was proposed, select Review proposed price and compare the proposal, active catalog price, difference, and calculated subtotal. Approve it unchanged or amend the unit price; an amendment requires an internal reason. Before issuing the quote, complete every non-billing readiness blocker, including activating a Customer administrator who can receive and approve it. Billing readiness may be completed after acceptance but is required before invoicing. The editor preselects the required PSeq Lab Service, explains that it is priced per specimen, and sets its read-only quantity from the Job's committed specimen count. The required line cannot be removed. Additional active catalog lines may be added with a per-unit price and a quantity chosen for that quote. Permanent accounting codes remain available in Order configuration but are not shown as quote-entry guidance. If the designated item is missing, inactive, or not priced per specimen, quote issuance is paused until Order configuration is corrected. POMS validates the item identity, unit, and committed quantity again on the server. POMS sends no Customer notice while a Phaeno-initiated Job remains Quote in preparation. Issuing or revising the quote rechecks ordering eligibility and the approver list, makes the quote available immediately, moves the Job to Quote issued, and notifies every active Customer administrator. The Customer can approve it; Phaeno cannot approve on the Customer's behalf. The accepting administrator becomes the Job's acting Customer contact for ordinary later notices. High-impact events, including cancellation by Phaeno and result release or payment hold, continue to notify all active Customer administrators.

sections.heading: Review the request
sections.text: Confirm that the Customer has an active laboratory-service entitlement and that the selected service is currently offered. Review the requested specimen count, each source group and count, shared handling and safety declarations, and Customer notes. Request a targeted correction when information is incomplete or unsafe rather than rewriting Customer data internally. Keep internal review notes separate from the tenant-safe reason shown to the Customer. The initial workflow is not a PHI intake path; do not ask for or store patient-identifying information.

sections.heading: Issue and accept the quote
sections.text: The Customer or Sales price proposal is part of the submitted request revision, not a quote. POMS preserves its unit price, note, proposer, and time. The issued quote records whether Phaeno approved that proposal or amended it, along with the responsible Commercial reviewer and decision time. When dual control is enabled, a Phaeno proposer cannot review the same proposal. The quote is a versioned, immutable Commercial offer for one job. Confirm the configured service, quantities, prices, currency, expected turnaround information, and expiration before issuance. Tax is calculated by POMS: when the complete billing and tax profile is Finance-approved, the quote includes and freezes tax; otherwise the quote is explicitly pre-tax and tax is calculated from the approved profile at invoicing. Saving the issued POMS quote makes it available for Customer acceptance. Cancel, Close, or Escape asks you to keep editing or discard unsaved quote changes. Dismissal is unavailable while the quote is being issued or its current record is being refreshed. A stale-record response preserves your entries; review the refreshed Job and pricing before deliberately submitting again. Customer acceptance performs one Commercial operation that: records the accepted quote revision and frozen pricing profile; and opens post-acceptance sample-list preparation. After the Customer enters or imports the exact compliant sample list, finalization atomically creates the immutable laboratory work authorization, linked Lab work order, shipment, and physical tube slots. Do not create a Lab work order manually if finalization fails. Resolve the reported roster or shipping-configuration issue and retry the durable operation. Physical samples must not arrive before quote acceptance and exact roster finalization create the authorized shipment. Quarantine and escalate an unexpected package under the approved receiving and custody exception. Do not accession, process, bill, or attach it to executable Job work.

sections.heading: Respect the Lab boundary
sections.text: After acceptance, Order Ops continues to own Customer communication, Commercial holds, cancellation review, billing, files, and publication. Open the linked work from the order or from Lab operations > Receipt & accession. Lab Ops owns return-kit preparation, shipment identification, receipt, accession, physical lineage, controlled execution, exceptions, and scientific approval. The Lab milestone Ready for release means the scientific gate passed. It does not upload, scan, attach, or publish a result. PSeq result publication still requires the governed file and release checks. PSeq scientific result release is independent of invoice balance, credit status, and payment; Partner workflows retain their separate commercial rules.

guides.title: Data assembly
guides.summary: Validate accepted inputs, record processing, and approve immutable output releases.

sections.heading: Partner data assembly
sections.text: Order Ops owns the Commercial Data Assembly order, quote, approval, cancellation, and accounting source record. Lab Ops owns input validation, processing milestones, quality review, and immutable output release. Inputs and outputs are manufacturing records; they are not source samples for Data Provisioning. Find the Commercial order in Order operations > Orders with order type Data Assembly. Open Lab operations > Data assembly to validate the submitted input and perform the manufacturing workflow. When Lab accepts the input, Commercial staff issue the quote from the linked order; manufacturing continues after Partner acceptance.

sections.heading: Validate the submission
sections.text: Confirm the active Partner, project reference, purchase-order requirement, selected active assembly profile, required metadata, and uploaded input revision. Validate file type, size, completeness, malware-scan state, and every profile-specific requirement. When the submission cannot pass input validation, Lab staff place the manufacturing record on hold and document the issue. Commercial staff use the linked order to request a targeted Customer correction or reject work that is unsafe, unsupported, or outside the offered profile. A correction creates a new input revision; it must not rewrite the revision that was reviewed previously.

sections.heading: Quote and accept the job
sections.text: Prepare the per-job quote from the current assembly offering and preserve its profile, price, currency, and expiration snapshot. Issuing the POMS quote makes it available to the Partner immediately. Acceptance records the immutable Commercial commitment and queues the work.

sections.heading: Process and review
sections.text: Record processing milestones against the accepted input revision and selected profile. Internal implementation details and intermediate files remain internal. When processing is complete, perform the configured quality review and document any hold or required correction.

sections.heading: Approve an output release
sections.text: An output release is immutable and identifies: the exact source input revision; the assembly profile and version; the output manifest and included files; checksums, scan state, and generation time; and the quality-review and approval facts. Approve a new release rather than replacing a prior release. POMS creates the accounting source record, then applies the Partner’s assembly-credit gate. Credit-approved work can be released under Net 30; work without approved credit remains on payment hold because manual payment confirmation is not yet implemented.

guides.title: Holds, cancellations, and adjustments
guides.summary: Pause work safely, decide cancellation requests, preserve completed work, and account for adjustments.

sections.heading: Holds, cancellations, and adjustments
sections.text: Holds and cancellation decisions preserve work already performed. They do not erase shipments, Lab execution, input revisions, output releases, Commercial documents, or audit history.

sections.heading: Place and release holds
sections.text: Phaeno may place an active workflow on hold for an operational, Commercial, validation, shipping, or Customer-action reason. Record a concise tenant-safe explanation and separate internal notes. A hold pauses the affected next action; it does not silently change quote, payment, scientific, or release state. Release a hold only after the blocking condition is resolved. The release is an audited Phaeno action and should reference the corrected fact or approved exception.

sections.heading: Handle cancellation timing
sections.text: A draft or other unaccepted commitment may be withdrawn under its workflow rules. After quote acceptance or reagent-order acceptance, cancellation becomes a request for Phaeno review. Decide the request as approved, partially approved, or declined based on work performed, material committed, quantities shipped, and outputs already released. For Customer laboratory work, Order Ops asks Lab Ops whether unreceived work can be cancelled before committing the Commercial decision. Started or specimen-level work requires a bounded manual decision; do not force Lab into a cancelled state.

sections.heading: Preserve unaffected work
sections.text: A partial cancellation can retain completed samples, shipped reagent quantities, or accepted assembly work while removing only the approved remainder. Preserve prior revisions, manifests, packing slips, releases, and Customer-visible history.

sections.heading: Record Commercial adjustments
sections.text: Record the portal cancellation decision without editing the original Commercial snapshot. Finance handles credits, revised invoices, taxes, freight, discounts, balances, and posting adjustments in the accounting system, using the POMS workflow references and stable journal-entry source IDs for reconciliation.

guides.title: Integration failures and recovery
guides.summary: Triage invitation, projection, result-pipeline, notification, and retained legacy-connector failures.

sections.heading: Accounting and notification recovery
sections.text: Order Ops uses durable invitation, notification, Lab projection, and provider-neutral result-pipeline records. A failed delivery remains attached to the original workflow with its idempotency key, attempt history, last error, and provider identifier when one exists. The retained accounting-connector queue is legacy/non-PSeq context; native PSeq AR remains local to POMS.

sections.heading: Triage the failure
sections.text: Open Attention for the owned cross-workflow exception or Legacy integrations for a retained connector/notification event. Identify the affected record, current delivery state, owner, age, attempts, next action, and tenant-visible consequence. Determine whether the local operation committed successfully before taking recovery action. Common states include: Invitation queued/failed/bounced/needs attention while access remains separately pending, accepted, expired, or revoked; Projection or scan failed while the immutable result package remains unreleased; failed notification delivery after the underlying portal action already succeeded.

sections.heading: Retry safely
sections.text: Refresh the workflow before investigating a missing accounting row. Do not recreate the order, quote, shipment, output approval, or result completion to force another row. Use the stable source ID when reconciling repeated report downloads. If an invitation hard-bounced, revoke and reissue to a corrected address rather than retrying it. If a pipeline submission or signed Mailgun webhook is replayed, use the stored idempotency/provider event identity rather than creating another package or delivery. If a notification failed, retry it without repeating the underlying business transition.

sections.heading: Communicate the boundary
sections.text: Keep operational state, accounting-source readiness, credit, file release, and notification delivery separate. An accounting question does not undo an issued quote or scientific completion. A failed email does not reverse the order action recorded in the portal. Escalate only after the operational record, report range, stable entry ID, and notification history have been reviewed. Include safe identifiers; never include credentials, payment data, or customer-confidential scientific detail in support notes.

guides.title: Order operations
guides.summary: Manage commercial intake, pricing, quotes, staging, governed PSeq release, native AR, and Partner workflows.

sections.heading: Order operations
sections.text: When starting a Customer Job, select the Customer department as well as the Company. A single available department is shown automatically. The department owns the Job and determines Customer access and the applicable service rule; a Blocked department rule cannot be bypassed by a Ready organization default. Order operations is the Commercial workspace for Customer laboratory orders, Partner PSeq kit fulfillment, and Partner data assembly. POMS owns operational state, assignments, tenant-safe communication, PSeq result release, and PSeq accounts receivable. Use the far-left sidebar beneath the toolbar to move among Order intake, Order staging, PSeq kits, Assembly, Attention, Result release, Finance, and Legacy integrations, subject to your explicit roles. Order intake combines sales handoffs, commercial review, pricing, and quotes in one active queue. Order staging shows every Customer and its readiness blockers; a Commercial Operator may prepare internal PSeq work before the Customer administrator is active when the stage-eligibility minimum is met. Quote issue and Customer commitment require all non-billing readiness items and an active Customer administrator. Billing readiness may be completed after acceptance but is required before invoicing. When the Portal API and frontend are both running in their local development environments, Simulate HubSpot handoff can create a durable pending request for either a sales-assisted order or a no-charge Trial Project. The simulator requires a unique HubSpot Deal identifier and clearly identifies the resulting request as simulated. It does not contact HubSpot, bypass review, create an executable sales-assisted order, or implement the Trial Project lifecycle. Review the resulting request in Accounts. The sidebar header identifies Order operations and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the edge tab. Choosing a section closes an unpinned sidebar.

sections.heading: Enter and find orders
sections.text: Order intake covers Customer and Partner commercial requests through review, pricing, quote issuance, and Customer acceptance. Accepted work leaves the active intake queue and continues in its owning Lab Operations queue. PSeq kits covers Partner order review, substitutions, backorders, shipments, and fulfillment. Assembly covers Partner intake validation, quoting, processing, quality review, and output release. Attention owns invitation, readiness, staged-order, projection/scan, unreleased-result, overdue-invoice, unapplied-cash, and reconciliation-difference exceptions. Result release publishes a scientifically approved, complete PSeq package per sample without a payment gate. Finance owns PSeq invoices, receipts/import, explicit allocation, aging, and reconciliation. Legacy integrations covers retained accounting-connector and notification recovery outside the active native PSeq AR workflow. Search Order intake by order, Job, Company, or request number. A PSeq Lab Service row identifies an optional proposed price so Commercial users can find pricing decisions without opening every record. On the order, Review proposed price compares the proposed USD price per specimen with the active catalog price, requested quantity, difference, and subtotal. Approve price and issue quote preserves the proposal unchanged; Amend price and issue quote requires an internal reason. Tax is system-calculated: include and freeze it when the billing and tax profile is complete and Finance-approved, or issue an explicitly pre-tax quote and calculate tax at invoicing. The issued quote, not the proposal, is the offer a Customer administrator may accept. The operational detail shows the current quote value, revision, and status. Internal context in the audit timeline explains Phaeno-only decisions; it is informational, not a Customer-facing warning. Assign an owner and due date when the workflow supports them. A queue assignment coordinates work; it does not grant authorization or change the workflow state.

sections.heading: Keep state boundaries visible
sections.text: Operational status, quote status, accounting-source readiness, payment, scientific readiness, file scanning, and publication are separate facts. Do not mark one complete merely because another succeeded. Tenant users receive a curated timeline, so record a tenant-safe reason separately from internal notes whenever an action can be seen outside Phaeno. Order Ops ends at the Commercial boundary for a Customer laboratory order: it remains in Order intake while pricing and quote decisions are active. After acceptance and exact sample-roster finalization authorize that work, use Lab Ops for return-kit preparation, shipment-packet and tube comparison, specimen receipt and accession, protocol execution, materials, equipment, libraries, batches, sequencing sendouts, exceptions, and scientific approval. The separate PSeq kits and Assembly sections continue to own their non-laboratory operational workflows. Lab readiness never publishes a file by itself.

sections.heading: Triage safely
sections.text: Confirm the active organization and workflow before opening a record. Review operational readiness, invitation delivery, scientific package, release, invoice, receipt, allocation, reconciliation, and notification states independently. Check open holds, cancellation requests, overdue actions, and failed deliveries. Assign the work and due date when ownership is unclear. Perform the smallest valid next action and preserve the existing record. POMS checks the latest Job immediately before issuing a quote. If the record changes after that check, POMS reloads it and preserves the entered quote lines; review those values, then issue the quote again. Never repair a failed workflow by creating a duplicate order, quote, invoice, receipt, result package, Lab work order, shipment, or release. Assign an attention item, preserve attempts, and record its resolution.

sections.heading: Review queued notifications
sections.text: Order notices check the current active organization, department, user, and administrator assignments when dispatched. The department notification address is included when configured; otherwise the organization notification default applies. An inactive or mismatched department cannot use either route. Review failed notices with no eligible recipients before retrying them; changing an assignment after a notice was queued changes who can receive it.

guides.title: PSeq kit fulfillment
guides.summary: Consume the Commercial order snapshot, manage substitutions and backorders, and ship immutably.

sections.heading: Partner reagent fulfillment
sections.text: Partner reagent orders use the offering and negotiated price available to the active Partner at placement. The placed order preserves an immutable Commercial snapshot even if catalog or pricing configuration changes later. Find the Commercial order in Order operations > Orders with order type PSeq Kit. Perform the Commercial review and order acceptance there. After acceptance, perform physical preparation, substitutions, shipping, and fulfillment in Lab operations > PSeq kits. The Lab workflow consumes the Commercial snapshot; it does not rewrite the ordered items or negotiated price.

sections.heading: Review a placed order
sections.text: Confirm the Partner, purchase-order number, shipping address, ordered items, selling units, quantities, negotiated prices, currency, and placement totals. Verify that the shipping destination and requested service satisfy the configured restrictions. In Order operations, move valid work through review and acceptance. Reject it with a Partner-safe reason when the address, eligibility, quantity, or Commercial facts require correction. Keep internal investigation details in the internal record. Lab staff see the order as awaiting Commercial review and cannot start fulfillment until it is accepted.

sections.heading: Handle substitutions and backorders
sections.text: Never substitute a different reagent silently. Record the original item, proposed item, quantity, price effect, and reason. A Partner administrator must explicitly approve the substitution. If the change increases the total, complete the required Commercial approval and preserve the adjustment for the manual accounting handoff before acceptance. Backorders remain part of the original order. Record the unshipped quantity and expected next action without changing quantities already shipped.

sections.heading: Create shipments
sections.text: Create a partial or complete shipment with: shipped quantities for each original order line; carrier, service, tracking number, and ship date; reagent lot or batch identifier; expiration date when the supplied reagent has one; and the packing-slip facts. Shipped quantities are immutable. Correct future fulfillment with a new shipment or documented adjustment; do not edit shipment history.

sections.heading: Complete fulfillment
sections.text: Reagent fulfillment creates a separate journal-entry source record for each shipment. Partial shipments therefore produce separate source rows tied to the same portal order. Finance completes invoice creation, account selection, tax treatment, and posting outside POMS. The order reaches fulfillment only when the accepted quantities are shipped, backordered quantities are resolved, and no blocking hold remains.

guides.title: Company access and user administration
guides.summary: Manage Company Portal requests, readiness, service entitlements, invitations, and access.

sections.heading: Company access and user administration
sections.text: Phaeno administrators manage Portal access, readiness, service entitlements, integration requests, and global access from the canonical CRM Company. Prospect, Customer, and Partner administrators manage membership only within their own access scope. Access is invitation-based and every durable administrative change is audited.

sections.heading: Know which administration surface owns each record
sections.text: The CRM Companies directory is the only customer directory. A Company may exist before Portal access is approved. After approval, the same Company workspace displays its relationship type, readiness, services, members, invitations, requests, and retention settings. The internal Organization identifier used for tenant isolation is not a second customer record and does not appear in a separate directory. User management is also connected to durable account APIs. In the Phaeno context, active accounts and invited people appear in one list alongside global account status and every enforced Phaeno role. A Pending invitation status means the recipient has not completed account registration. Open a card’s actions menu to edit an active user, deactivate another active user, reactivate a disabled user, or resend or revoke a pending invitation. A Phaeno administrator cannot deactivate their own account. Edit one active user to update their name, Platform administrator assignment, and additive laboratory roles together. Platform administrators retain bootstrap access to every laboratory capability even when no explicit laboratory role is assigned. The role picker contains only roles enforced by the current authorization model: Platform administrator, Lab operator, Lab supervisor, Protocol administrator, Scientific reviewer, and Lab operations administrator. Authentication-provider metadata and unsupported job-title labels do not grant Portal access. Cards marked Pending invitation still represent invitation records, not accepted user records. Enter the person’s first name, last name, and exact sign-in email, then select the Platform administrator and additive laboratory roles they should receive. The pending role intent grants no access. It becomes active only when the recipient accepts and becomes an active Phaeno member.

sections.heading: Review and maintain Companies
sections.text: Create the Company first, then request the approved Portal relationship when access is needed: Prospect for an external organization that may receive explicitly granted curated data but cannot order work. Customer for organizations that request laboratory services. Partner for organizations that submit specimens for PSeq Lab Service or purchase the PSeq Kit, which includes data assembly. Phaeno for internal platform operations. Do not use Company lifecycle or Portal readiness as a shortcut for access. Curated package access requires an exact-version grant, member access requires an accepted invitation, and commercial work requires a current service entitlement. Open CRM and select Companies to search durable external customer records. Select the Company name to open its workspace. Use its Requests tab to propose online access, a product or service change, a relationship change, or reviewed work. Use CRM's central Requests section for requests that still need a Phaeno decision. The Company tab preserves request history but does not duplicate the decision controls. There is no standalone customer-creation action outside CRM. For a pending onboarding or evaluation request, select Approve and enable Portal access and record the approval reason. POMS atomically approves the request, creates the Company's internal tenant scope with Pending readiness, and attaches it to the existing Company. Online-access approval never adds or removes a product or service entitlement, creates another customer record, or creates a user. If an older approved onboarding or evaluation request shows Portal access incomplete, select Complete Portal access. POMS creates and attaches the missing tenant scope without changing product or service entitlements. This recovery does not create another Company, invite users, create an order, or complete the request. If POMS finds an active, compatible access scope with the exact Company name that is not linked to another Company, it pauses and shows Existing access scope found. Review the displayed name and relationship, then select Use existing access scope to reconnect it. Reuse preserves existing users, orders, invitations, and history. Existing Company requests are attached to the scope so they can be fulfilled through their separate owning workflows; attaching them does not grant product or service access. POMS will not offer this shortcut when the scope is inactive, belongs to another Company, or has a different relationship kind; resolve those cases before approving access. Record readiness as Not reviewed, Pending, Ready, or Blocked, with an internal note when useful. Readiness describes operational setup; it does not invite a user, activate a service, or place an order.

sections.heading: Review Company requests
sections.text: Use CRM's central Requests section to decide pending onboarding, evaluation, product and service, relationship, sales-assisted order, and offboarding requests created by the first-party CRM. Approved requests remain available in the Company's Requests tab as history. An approved online-access request without its tenant scope remains in the queue only as a recovery exception. Historical HubSpot-sourced requests remain readable, but no HubSpot intake or simulation endpoint is part of the standalone workflow. Approve or decline a pending request with a reason. For onboarding or evaluation, approval also creates and attaches the Company's pending-readiness access scope while leaving product and service entitlements unchanged. Other request types record the decision only. Complete each approved invitation, entitlement, or order change through its owning workflow, verify the outcome, and then select Complete request in the central Requests queue and record what was completed. Never put specimen, scientific, downstream-customer, credential, or other sensitive operational details in an external reference or request summary.

sections.heading: Invite administrators and members
sections.text: From Company detail, open People. Start with the reviewed CRM Contact, select Invite to Portal, and choose the Departments the person may access. Assign organization-wide administrator access only when the person must govern every Department; otherwise use Department membership and grant Department administrator access only where needed. A CRM Contact remains separate from a Portal user and grants no access until the invitation is accepted. Ask the recipient to sign in with the invited email and accept the Portal invitation. Use Departments & services to create or rename operational units, choose the default, record typed configuration overrides, and manage Department membership. Every Organization begins with General. Organization administrators can edit the five Organization defaults for PO, billing and notification email, shipping, and result instructions. A blank Department override inherits the Organization default, then the commercial profile or system rule. The system PO rule is not required; either level can explicitly require or waive it. Existing saved shipping and accepted-quote snapshots retain their values. Result-delivery instructions are retained with the commercial commitment, not an automatic change to storage destinations. Organization administrators can access every active Department; other users must retain at least one active Department assignment. When one business unit must not be discoverable or governed by another—or it has separate contracting, tax, legal, ownership, or retention obligations—create a separate Company/Organization instead of a Department. External Organization and Department administrators can use Departments in the user menu. Organization administrators own structure, default selection, lifecycle, organization defaults, new invitations, and organization roles. Department administrators own settings and member access only within assigned Departments. Add existing members by exact email lookup; review each assignment or role change. One person may administer Research, belong to Operations as a member, and have no Finance access. Rights remain independent in each Organization. Department changes use review dialogs. Deactivation requires affected active members to have another Department assignment and retains historical records. Reactivation does not restore revoked assignments automatically. Changing the default affects future default selections, not existing records or memberships. A conflict reloads the latest Department version while preserving your form entries for review. Contact invitation access must still be valid when the invitation is resent or accepted; if the Contact or Department changed, review and reissue the invitation. Service entitlements and curated-data packages may be organization-wide or limited to one Department. A Department-specific service entitlement takes precedence over the Organization default for that Department. In Data provisioning, choose an explicit access scope when assigning a package; users in other Departments cannot list or download that Department's grant. Users with more than one available Department select the working Department from the user menu. The header shows the Organization and Department currently in force. Do not rely on a browser URL or a previously opened page to establish access; the API validates both scopes on every protected operation. Do not create a normal membership directly. Invitation acceptance provides the user-facing consent point and the audit link between invitation, user, and membership. For an internal employee, select the Phaeno organization and open User management. Use Add Phaeno user, enter the person’s first name, last name, and exact sign-in email, and select the narrowest roles needed for their work. Grant Platform administrator only when platform-wide administration is required. The card remains marked Pending invitation until acceptance; afterward, open its actions menu and choose Edit whenever the profile or roles must change. To follow up before acceptance, find the card marked Pending invitation, open its actions menu, and choose Resend invitation. Resending rotates the private link and is subject to a cooldown. Revoke an invitation that should not be accepted. In local development, a Company's Users section also provides Create sign-in link after Portal access is enabled. It replaces the prior invitation link and displays a fresh link that you can copy into a private window. On the invitation page, choose Sign in or create account; if the fake email does not yet exist in the Clerk development instance, choose Sign up, create it with that exact invited email, and then accept the invitation. This development control is not available in production. Use it only with fake development accounts, and do not put a real invitation link into tickets or documentation.

sections.heading: Convert a Prospect
sections.text: Convert a Prospect access relationship to Customer or Partner only after the business relationship is approved. Conversion preserves the Company, internal access identifier, users, memberships, grants, and audit history. It does not create an order, assign broad data access, or configure prices automatically. After conversion, complete the applicable operational setup: analysis availability and Customer credit for a Customer, or offerings, negotiated reagent pricing, assembly profiles, and Partner assembly credit for a Partner.

sections.heading: Manage service entitlements
sections.text: From the Company, open Departments & services, then select Services to record dated commercial permission: Customers may receive PSeq Lab Service. Partners may receive PSeq Lab Service and PSeq Kit. Prospects and Phaeno organizations do not receive commercial service entitlements. Set configuration to Pending, Ready, or Blocked. A service is usable only when its entitlement is effective and configuration is Ready. Overlapping periods for the same service are rejected. If a service already has a non-ended entitlement, select Edit on that entitlement instead of adding another overlapping period. Preserve the service and existing effective date unless the commercial authorization changed, set the current configuration, attach the eligible approved source request, and save. Editing updates the existing audited record; it does not create a duplicate. Ended historical entitlements remain read-only. Online access does not imply a product or service entitlement. Add a dated entitlement here only after the corresponding product or service authorization is approved. When the entitlement implements an approved Portal request, select that request as its source. The selector shows only approved or applied requests for this organization that include the selected service. Leave the source blank only for a documented manual exception; do not attach an onboarding-only request to a service entitlement. Use End now instead of deleting an entitlement. Review the consequence dialog and record why the entitlement is ending. The Portal retains and displays that reason with the ended entitlement. PSeq Kit includes kit fulfillment followed by data submission and assembly. Do not create a separate data-assembly entitlement or sell data assembly without the kit.

sections.heading: Deactivate and restore access
sections.text: Deactivate a membership in Company detail to remove one access relationship. Deactivate the Company when none of its memberships should be usable; this suspends its attached Portal access scope. Reactivating the Company restores that scope. Each action opens a consequence dialog; verify the named Company or person before confirming. A deactivated membership is restored through a fresh invitation and acceptance. When all Portal access for another person must stop, select Deactivate on that Phaeno user and confirm the named person. The account, memberships, assigned roles, and audit history remain, but the user immediately loses effective access. A Phaeno administrator cannot deactivate their own account. Use Reactivate to restore an authorized disabled account; then review its memberships and roles before considering access complete. Preserve historical records; do not delete users, memberships, or organizations to resolve access problems.

sections.heading: Triage access safely
sections.text: Confirm the person’s email, session state, selected organization, active membership, role, and organization status. Use record identifiers and audit events to trace changes. Do not ask for passwords, sign-in codes, invitation tokens, browser storage, or another tenant’s records. For a user who has lost both the authenticator and all one-time backup codes, verify the person's identity and organization through the approved support procedure. In Clerk, reset the user's MFA enrollments and revoke every active session. Record the administrative recovery without storing codes, authenticator secrets, or recovery links. Tell the user to sign in again and connect a new authenticator; required MFA keeps the session pending until enrollment is complete. An email request starts the review but is not sufficient by itself to authorize the reset. If two administrators update the same record, the portal can reject the stale action. Reload the latest version, review the intervening change, and then make a deliberate new update rather than overwriting it.

guides.title: Statuses and recovery
guides.summary: Triage operational states and safely recover accounting records, files, releases, and notifications.

sections.heading: Statuses and recovery
sections.text: Treat operational work, accounting source records, notifications, file scanning, and file release as separate lifecycles. Recover the failed lifecycle without rewriting accepted scope or creating duplicate records.

sections.heading: Triage order operations
sections.text: Use Customer lab, Partner reagent, and Partner assembly queues to find work by its current status. Prioritize: scan or safety failures that block intake or release; payment or release-state conflicts that affect a ready result; missing or unexpected accounting source records; Customer- or Partner-visible holds and requested corrections; notifications that remain pending or failed. The overall order status is not sufficient evidence. Check sample or shipment progress, the current quote, commercial document, scan state, release state, cancellation request, and notification record separately.

sections.heading: Recover Lab projections and exceptions
sections.text: Lab execution events are delivered durably to Commercial projections. If a Customer milestone, schedule, action request, or permitted QC summary is delayed, verify the Lab work order and event state, then retry the existing delivery path. Do not recreate the authorization, create a second work order, or copy Laboratory facts directly into Commercial records. Internal and Customer-action-required exceptions are separate. Resolve the existing blocking exception with an authorized Supervisor action and a retained resolution note. Never copy an internal investigation description into the Customer-safe summary. Ready for release is a scientific milestone only; recover file scanning, payment, and publication through their own lifecycles.

sections.heading: Review manual accounting source records
sections.text: POMS creates stable journal-entry source rows at the implemented billing boundaries. The report itself does not post entries or choose general-ledger accounts. Open Order operations, then Accounting. Select the inclusive accounting-date range. Compare the organization, workflow number, source document, reference, currency, gross amount, and balance with the operational record. Download the CSV and complete account selection, tax treatment, and posting in the accounting system. Preserve the stable entry ID during reconciliation; downloading the same range again does not mark a source row as posted. QuickBooks Online integration is deferred. Historical integration messages cannot be retried, and the manual source report is not a payment-confirmation workflow.

sections.heading: Recover files and releases
sections.text: Files progress through Pending, Scanning, Clean, Rejected, Failed, or Unavailable scan states. Only clean files can continue to a valid release state. Investigate a rejected scan as a safety event; do not mark it clean manually. Retry a failed or unavailable scan only after the scanner or storage dependency is healthy. Keep output Internal while review is incomplete. Use Ready when operational review is complete, Payment hold when commercial release is blocked, and Released only when every applicable gate passes. Use Withdrawn when a previously available file must no longer be delivered; preserve the record and audit history. Credit approval permits Net 30 release for the applicable Customer lab or Partner assembly workflow. Without credit, files remain on payment hold until a separately approved payment-confirmation workflow is implemented. Do not use an order-status change to bypass this rule.

sections.heading: Recover notifications
sections.text: Notification records use Pending, Sending, Sent, and Failed. Correct the delivery configuration or address, then retry the existing durable message. Confirm the final delivery state and avoid sending a separate untracked message as though it were the portal notification.

sections.heading: Respect terminal and superseded states
sections.text: Do not retry business actions that are rejected, declined, cancelled, withdrawn, or based on an expired or superseded quote. Start the documented replacement workflow when new scope, a new quote, or a corrected input revision is required. For escalation, record the portal identifiers, lifecycle and visible status, safe error category, timestamps, retry count, and whether the external dependency is healthy. Keep credentials, webhook secrets, access tokens, Customer-confidential data, protected health information, and raw scientific files out of tickets and browser-bundled documentation.

guides.title: Trial Projects
guides.summary: Scope, approve, execute, release, and close Trial Projects using existing PSeq workflows.

sections.heading: Operate Trial Projects
sections.text: Trial Projects provide no-charge, closed-ended PSeq evaluations of extracted RNA. POMS owns the scientific scope, approvals, sample authorization, laboratory execution, and release. CRM owns the commercial request and follow-up. Trial work creates no order, quote, invoice, payment gate, or QuickBooks transaction. For Research Use Only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures. Never request PHI. Use coded sample references, and keep suspected prohibited information out of ordinary notes, notifications, and CRM summaries. Place affected Trial work on hold and follow the authorized incident process when prohibited information is suspected.

sections.heading: Prepare the commercial request and scope
sections.text: From a CRM Company's Requests tab, create a Work → Trial Project request linked to an active Opportunity. Include commercial context only. Prepare the Company's active Prospect Portal access and department through the separate access workflow. A CRM request or an approved access request does not approve scientific Trial work. Select Start Trial beside the Company's request to carry that request into Trial creation and retain a route back to the Company. From Trial projects, you can also search and page through eligible requests. A request can create only one Trial; its link opens the existing workspace once started. Select Define scope. The dedicated scope page captures the objective, numeric original sample allowance, explicit submission window, current production PSeq workflow, active PSeq analysis definitions, and versioned deliverables. FASTQ, FASTA, and BAM are configurable initial defaults. Select the deliverables required for this evaluation; approved scopes preserve the selected definitions and versions. Record RNA submission instructions, success criteria, Prospect terms, residual-material retention and disposition, and internal estimated retail value and anticipated cost. Return arrangements require destination, handling, and shipping payer. They become immutable after the first sample submission. Internal costs never appear in the Prospect view.

sections.heading: Assign and record approval responsibilities
sections.text: Trial configuration shows primary and delegated authorities by Commercial and Scientific Operations domain. A Phaeno platform administrator assigns or revokes the primary approvers; the defaults are the CBO and COO responsibilities. Each primary may explicitly designate and revoke delegates for their own domain. Revoking a primary also revokes their delegates. Past decisions remain intact. Each scope revision needs two affirmative decisions from two different people. A person authorized in both domains cannot approve both sides of the same revision. Request changes requires a new scope revision. Amend scope preserves the previous scope and requires two new approvals plus Prospect organization-administrator acceptance. Scientific Operations authorities maintain the versioned deliverable catalog. Defining a revision retires the previous definition for new selection. Retiring a deliverable does not rewrite approved scopes.

sections.heading: Execute the approved work
sections.text: The Prospect organization administrator accepts the approved RUO/no-PHI terms and submits samples during the agreed window. Department administrators cannot substitute for that role. Submit samples lets the administrator prepare a roster sharing one RNA type and shipping destination; submitting the roster creates one authorization and shipment. Each sample checks allowance, extracted-RNA metadata, approved analysis inputs, configured quantity units and limits, and active shipping instructions. The form identifies concentration and other inputs required by the approved analyses. Changed forms ask before discarding entries, including when leaving the scope page. During a save or explicit reload, editing, repeat actions, and dismissal are blocked until the operation finishes. The scope page also protects navigation while reloading. Reload current Trial; keep my entries refreshes scope-dependent choices and preserves entries for review, including when the reload fails; a changed scope requires a fresh acceptance confirmation. The shared Lab Operations provider creates Trial-authorized work pinned to the approved workflow version. Existing registered-tube, packet, receipt, accession, protocol, QC, sequencing, and scientific-review controls apply. Use Shipping and packets and each sample's Open laboratory work link. Trial holds and approval changes stop scientific progress and shipping mutations; custody facts and exception handling remain recordable. Schedule estimate communicates an estimate without changing scope. Authorize replacement records the failed sample, responsibility, reason, and approving authority. It permits exactly one replacement and never increases the frozen original allowance. Prospect-caused problems need the same explicit exception approval.

sections.heading: Review and release results
sections.text: The governed PSeq pipeline supplies immutable output packages tied to the Trial, submitted sample, and Lab work order. Complete checksums and clean scans precede scientific review. Scientific approval and release retain the existing PSeq separation of duties. A release manager selects one scientifically approved package per sample, with every frozen deliverable and no unapproved output role. Choose Partial when only some approved results are ready. Choose Complete only when the full approved package for every submitted sample, including approved replacements, is available. A complete release closes the Trial and freezes the shared global/organization retention policy. No payment or credit gate applies. The result archive includes a Trial manifest with the exact RUO statement, scope revision, sample/file lineage, and checksums. After complete release, earlier partial archives remain historical and direct members to the current complete package. Download controls show progress and availability, including closed retention access, and refresh after transfer attempts. Internal downloads do not satisfy the organization's retention condition. Retention and receipt supports the shared warning, grace, hold, deletion, and reissue workflow. A complete reissue after byte deletion requires newly transferred, scientifically approved packages for the same Trial samples and retains the original closure/material dates. Release and physical shipping remain subject to configured operational readiness. A visible workflow or a passing software test does not activate real storage, scanning, automated byte deletion, or validate laboratory packing instructions.

sections.heading: Close and follow up
sections.text: Successful completion is recorded by complete result release. Otherwise use Close Trial with the appropriate outcome and a Prospect-safe reason. Closure blocks new submissions and requests cancellation of unfinished Lab authorizations while preserving custody and history. Residual RNA retention starts at terminal closure. Record material disposition records actual exhaustion, return, or destruction once under the frozen terms; a due date does not record physical destruction automatically. A hold blocks disposition. Commercial outcome is separate: schedule owned and dated follow-up, record closed without conversion, or record conversion only after the explicit CRM relationship workflow changes the same organization to Customer or Partner. Conversion never extends Trial file deadlines or starts new Trial work. Use the existing organization closeout workflow for any deliberate deactivation after reviewing other active Trials, grants, and relationships. Trial milestones publish to CRM as relationship-safe summaries and a deep link. Scientific details and sample identifiers stay in the Trial/Lab workspaces. Failed publication retries without blocking Trial operations; the Trial workspace shows pending milestones and provides Retry CRM publication.

sections.heading: Close Prospect access
sections.text: After all Trial and commercial evaluation work is closed without conversion, a platform administrator can use Close Prospect access in the Trial. The action requires a reason and checks all Company Trials, holds, open Opportunities, data grants, and service access. Resolve those relationships before retrying. This deactivates the Company and Prospect organization while preserving Trial history and existing retention deadlines. Byte deletion never performs this deactivation automatically.

guides.title: Account and access
guides.summary: Accept invitations, complete MFA, confirm the current organization, understand roles, and resolve access problems.

sections.heading: Account and access
sections.text: Your Portal access is created through an invitation to a specific Prospect organization. The current organization, your active membership, and your role determine which data and administrative information is available.

sections.heading: Accept an invitation
sections.text: Open the newest invitation link sent for your Prospect organization. Sign in with the same email address that received the invitation. Review the organization, your name, and the offered role. Accept or decline the invitation. The invitation page shows the email address currently signed in. If it is not the invited email, choose Sign out and use invited email, then sign in with the correct account. The invitation remains available in that browser while you switch accounts, and the identity service returns you to the invitation page after sign-in or account creation. Invitation links are private. A link can expire, be revoked, or be replaced by a newer invitation. If it is unavailable, ask your organization administrator or Phaeno to send a new invitation. The portal does not collect or reset your sign-in password. Use the account recovery offered by the identity service on the sign-in page.

sections.heading: Protect your account
sections.text: After your first sign-in step, connect an authenticator app and confirm the code it displays. Save the one-time backup codes shown during setup somewhere private and separate from the device running the authenticator. Never send an authenticator or backup code to Phaeno or your organization administrator. If you lose the authenticator but still have a backup code, use that code to sign in, then contact Phaeno to reset the authenticator enrollment. If you lose both the authenticator and every backup code, contact Phaeno directly. Phaeno will verify your identity and organization before resetting MFA; all active sessions are revoked and you must connect a new authenticator before Portal access resumes. Email can start the support request but does not itself bypass MFA.

sections.heading: Confirm the current organization
sections.text: The user menu shows the organization active in your current session. Every package, download, and administrative view is scoped to it. Self-service switching between multiple external organization memberships is not currently available. If the wrong organization is shown, stop and contact Phaeno before opening or downloading data.

sections.heading: Work within a department
sections.text: The header identifies your current organization and department. If you have access to more than one department, open the user menu and choose Department before opening or creating work. With a single available department, it is selected for you. Changing departments closes the previous workspace; finish or save your work before switching. Members see only their assigned departments. Organization administrators can select any active department in their organization, but the selected department still determines the records displayed. A department administrator's operational authority applies only to that department; it is not organization-wide access. Organization-wide data grants may be available in each department. If a department is unavailable or an expected Prospect record is missing, ask your organization administrator or Phaeno to review the assignment. Do not change URLs to try to access another department. Organization and department administrators can open Departments from the user menu to manage the departments within their authority.

sections.heading: Manage department access and settings
sections.text: Organization administrators manage all departments, organization defaults, the default department, and department lifecycle. Department administrators manage settings and member access only in their assigned departments. A person can be an administrator in Research and a member in Operations; granting one department role does not grant organization-wide administrator rights. In Departments, use a department's actions menu to Edit settings or Manage members. To add an existing organization member, enter their exact email, choose Find member, and review the access change before confirming. Only an organization administrator can invite someone new through User management or change an organization role. Organization administrators already have access to every department and cannot be restricted by a department admin. An active member must retain at least one active department assignment. Organization administrators use Edit organization defaults to set the purchase-order rule, billing and notification email, and shipping and result instructions. A department override takes precedence; a blank override inherits the organization value, then the existing system or commercial fallback. Saved shipping and accepted-quote snapshots retain their recorded values. Result instructions do not change the storage destination or grant an ordering service. Invitations require reviewed department access for members. Select each department and grant its administrator role only when needed. Organization administrators receive access to every department, including future additions. If settings changed while you were editing, review your preserved entries against the latest version before saving again. Closing an unsaved form asks whether to discard the changes.

sections.heading: Understand roles
sections.text: Member can review and download package versions explicitly granted to the current Prospect organization. Organization administrator can also review organization download history and respond to applicable package-governance instructions. Prospect organization administrators manage membership only for their current organization. In User management, active members and invited people appear in one list. A Pending invitation status means account registration is incomplete. Use the card’s actions menu to resend or revoke that invitation, edit an active member’s organization role, or deactivate another member’s membership. An administrator cannot deactivate their own membership from User management. Restoring a deactivated membership requires a fresh invitation and acceptance. Contact Phaeno for a globally disabled account or an action the organization administrator cannot complete.

sections.heading: Resolve common access states
sections.text: | What you see | What to do | | --- | --- | | Access unavailable after sign-in | Choose Continue invitation if it is shown, then review and accept the saved invitation. Otherwise, sign out and reopen the newest invitation link. | | Invitation link unavailable | Ask an administrator to confirm that the invitation is still pending and resend it. Use only the newest link. | | Email does not match | Sign out and use the email address that received the invitation, or request a corrected invitation. | | No active memberships | Ask your Prospect administrator to coordinate a fresh invitation with Phaeno. | | Wrong organization shown | Stop before opening data and contact Phaeno to verify the active membership. | | Organization unavailable | Ask Phaeno whether the organization is inactive. | | Account disabled | Contact Phaeno. A Prospect administrator cannot override a globally disabled account. | | Authenticator lost, backup code available | Use one backup code to sign in, then contact Phaeno for an MFA reset. | | Authenticator and backup codes lost | Contact Phaeno for identity verification and an MFA reset. Do not send old codes. | Never send a password, sign-in code, invitation token, or browser storage value in a support message.

guides.title: Data governance and downloads
guides.summary: Understand revocation, quarantine, retirement, download history, and safe governance responses.

sections.heading: Data governance and downloads
sections.text: Phaeno may revoke a grant, quarantine a package version, or retire a package as scientific, contractual, or governance needs change. These controls stop future portal access but cannot recall files that were already downloaded.

sections.heading: Respond to a package notice
sections.text: When Phaeno sends a package-governance instruction: Confirm the package name and exact version. Stop new use or distribution when the notice requires it. Follow the safe action stated by Phaeno for copies already held by your organization. If an attestation is requested, an organization administrator should record the organization’s response in the portal. Do not include downloaded data, confidential scientific content, credentials, or internal investigation details in an attestation or support message.

sections.heading: Understand package states
sections.text: | State or event | Effect on your organization | | --- | --- | | Grant revoked | Future access to the granted package version stops. Earlier downloads are not recalled. | | Version quarantined | Future access is blocked while Phaeno investigates or resolves the issue. | | Package retired | The package is no longer available for new use through the portal. | | New version published | Existing grants do not move automatically; Phaeno must grant the new version separately. |

sections.heading: Review download history
sections.text: Organization and department administrators can review curated download history for the selected department. This includes downloads from packages shared across the organization. Organization administrators can switch departments to review each department's activity. Department administrators see only activity within their assigned departments. Older download records without a recorded department remain available only to organization administrators, for organization-wide grants or grants assigned to the selected department. Changing a person's department assignments does not move or erase their earlier download records. Use download history to determine which package version and file were downloaded, by whom, and when. Download history does not prove that every local copy was deleted or that downstream use stopped; follow your organization’s governance process and any instruction from Phaeno. Phaeno retains audit history for grants, downloads, and governance actions. Do not ask support to delete history to conceal an access or download event. Safety and withdrawal instructions about previously supplied data continue to go to current organization administrators during an organization suspension. These notices do not restore Portal access. Contact Phaeno if you cannot record a required response in the portal.

guides.title: Use the Data Library
guides.summary: Review explicitly granted package versions and verify file or archive downloads.

sections.heading: Use the Data Library
sections.text: The Data Library is a read-only catalog of Phaeno-owned curated data package versions explicitly granted to your Prospect organization. A grant applies only to the named package version; access to one version does not automatically include earlier or later versions.

sections.heading: Review a granted package
sections.text: Open Data Library in the current Prospect organization. Select a package to review its summary and granted version. Review the manifest, file names, sizes, and checksums before downloading. Download an individual file or the package archive when needed. Preserve the package version and checksum with your internal record of the download. The package summary and manifest describe the curated release. They do not create a service request, place an order, or authorize use beyond the terms agreed with Phaeno.

sections.heading: Understand access boundaries
sections.text: Phaeno must explicitly grant each package version to the organization. A newly published version does not replace or extend an existing grant. Members of another organization cannot use your organization’s grant. The portal does not allow a Prospect to upload, edit, publish, or grant packages. Download activity is recorded for governance and support. If a package you expected is absent, provide Phaeno with the organization, package name, and expected version.
