Do not request access by sending copied data or another organization’s package details.

sections.heading: Verify a download
sections.text: Use the displayed checksum to verify that a downloaded file or archive is complete and unchanged. If a checksum does not match, delete the incomplete copy and retry once. If the second download also fails, stop and contact Phaeno with the package version, file name, time of the attempt, and the safe error message shown by the portal.

guides.title: Getting started
guides.summary: Confirm the current organization, understand Prospect access, and find granted data.

sections.heading: Getting started
sections.text: Portal gives a Prospect organization access to explicitly granted Phaeno-owned curated data and approved Trial Projects. Trial organization administrators can accept frozen scope and submit coded research RNA under the approved allowance and dates. Prospect access does not include laboratory requests, reagent orders, data-assembly requests, or other commercial ordering.

sections.heading: Navigate the help center
sections.text: Guide navigation opens beneath the toolbar from the far-left edge of the screen. Its header identifies Documentation and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the tab. Choosing a guide closes an unpinned sidebar and displays the article.

sections.heading: Confirm the current organization
sections.text: The user menu shows the organization active in your current session. That organization controls every record and action you can see, and information never carries between organizations. Self-service switching between multiple external organization memberships is not currently available. If the wrong organization is active, or your account belongs to more than one external organization, contact Phaeno before continuing.

sections.heading: Know your access level
sections.text: Active Prospect members can review and download the exact curated package versions granted to their organization. Organization administrators can also review organization download history and may be asked to respond to a package-governance notice. Prospect organization administrators use User management for durable invitations, Member or Organization administrator roles, and membership deactivation. Other members do not receive those controls.

sections.heading: Find your work
sections.text: Dashboard shows live organization-scoped counts and starting points for assigned data, authorized Trial Project shipments, and administrator user access. Trial Projects opens approved scope, sample submission, laboratory progress, released results, and retention receipts. Read Trial Projects before accepting a scope. Data Library contains curated package versions explicitly granted to the Prospect. Samples & shipping contains authorized Trial Project return kits, tube matching, and shipping packets when Phaeno has prepared a shipment. For organization administrators, User management manages organization invitations, roles, and memberships. Docs opens these Prospect guides. Prospect organizations do not receive order or service workspaces. Phaeno alone can change the organization relationship after business approval.

sections.heading: Get help safely
sections.text: When contacting Phaeno, provide the organization name, package name and version, and a description of the step you were performing. Do not send passwords, sign-in codes, invitation links, authentication tokens, or downloaded data in a support message.

sections.heading: Search and browse guides
sections.text: Use Search documentation at the top of Docs to find a guide or a matching section. Results update after a short pause; use at least two characters. Try “Trial acceptance” or “download grace”. Choose Filters to narrow results by Topic, Workflow, or Guide type. Clear filters removes those selections. Browse by topic opens guides for a topic without requiring search words. Workflow links and Related guides at the end of an article provide other ways to find relevant instructions. Select a result title to open its matching section. Your browser’s Back action restores the search and filters. Search uses the guides for your current organization; it does not include the public Website or operational records. A guide’s instructions do not change your account permissions. If no guides match, try fewer words or clear the filters. If search is temporarily unavailable, use Try again or Browse all guides. A documentation update may require Refresh page; guide browsing remains available while the update finishes.

guides.title: Organization access and transition
guides.summary: Understand membership boundaries and what changes when Phaeno converts a Prospect relationship.

sections.heading: Organization access and transition
sections.text: A Prospect is a tenant-isolated external organization that may receive explicitly granted curated data but cannot place commercial orders. Its users, memberships, grants, downloads, and audit history remain scoped to that organization.

sections.heading: Manage organization access
sections.text: Organization administrators manage access from User management. Enter the person’s first name, last name, and exact sign-in email, then choose Member or Organization administrator. Invited people appear in the same list with a Pending invitation status. Open a card’s actions menu to resend or revoke an invitation, edit an active member’s organization role, or deactivate another member’s organization membership. An administrator cannot deactivate their own membership from User management. Never copy or request an invitation token. A deactivated membership is restored only through a fresh invitation and acceptance. Contact Phaeno when the entire user account is disabled or when an invitation or membership action cannot be completed.

sections.heading: Understand a relationship change
sections.text: Only Phaeno can convert a Prospect organization to Customer or Partner, and only after the business relationship is approved. Conversion preserves the organization identifier, users, memberships, package grants, download history, and audit history. Conversion does not automatically: create or authorize an order; grant additional package versions; configure prices, credit, offerings, or analyses; accept commercial terms on the organization’s behalf; or change a user’s role. After conversion, Phaeno completes the applicable service and commercial setup before order actions become available. Until then, continue to use only the capabilities visible in the portal.

sections.heading: Protect organization boundaries
sections.text: Do not use another organization’s invitation, package link, downloaded file, or commercial reference. If the current organization name is wrong, stop before opening data and contact Phaeno.

guides.title: Prepare and ship samples
guides.summary: Associate Phaeno-supplied tube barcodes with your sample identifiers, retain the crosswalk, and ship an authorized Trial Project package.

sections.heading: Prepare and ship Trial Project samples
sections.text: When Phaeno makes an accepted Trial Project shipment available, open Samples & shipping. The shipment shows the Phaeno return kit, expected samples, destination, and current packet status. Phaeno creates and approves scope in Trial Projects. A Prospect organization administrator accepts it and submits coded samples there before this shared shipment is authorized. See Trial Projects.

sections.heading: Keep your records connected to the tubes
sections.text: Each Phaeno-supplied tube has a permanent manufacturer barcode. Your organization administrator scans or enters that barcode beside the correct Customer sample identifier before anything is shipped. Use a stable, non-PHI identifier that your organization can connect to its own sample record. Do not enter a patient name, medical-record number, date of birth, or other direct identifier. Phaeno preserves the tube-to-sample crosswalk in the Portal and in the shipment packet. Download the CSV or print the packet for your records. Your organization remains responsible for knowing what its Customer sample identifier means; Phaeno is responsible for retaining the identifier-to-tube association used for shipping and intake. If the wrong tube was assigned, an organization administrator can scan the replacement tube and record why the assignment changed. The earlier association remains in history. If a packet was already confirmed, saving the correction before shipment voids that packet and issues a corrected revision; destroy any unused copy of the old packet and print the replacement. Do not cover, alter, or remove the manufacturer barcode.

sections.heading: Confirm and ship
sections.text: Assign exactly one registered tube from the displayed return kit to every expected sample. Confirm the crosswalk only after checking every row. POMS then freezes the destination, instructions, manifest, packet barcode, and tube-to-sample crosswalk for that packet revision. Print the full packet. Follow the preparation and packing instructions, place the manifest inside the package, and use the ship-to page with the carrier label. The Phaeno packet barcode does not buy postage and is not a tube barcode. After handing the package to the carrier, record the carrier, tracking number, and shipment time in Samples & shipping. If a tube cannot be matched confidently or its barcode will not scan, stop and contact Phaeno instead of guessing.

guides.title: Statuses and troubleshooting
guides.summary: Resolve common grant, package, download, checksum, organization, and access problems.

sections.heading: Statuses and troubleshooting
sections.text: Use the visible organization, package version, grant state, and safe portal message to understand a problem before contacting Phaeno. | What you see | Meaning | What to do | | --- | --- | --- | | No packages | No active package version is currently granted to the organization, or the expected grant is unavailable. | Confirm the organization shown in the user menu, then ask Phaeno to review the exact package version. | | Package or version missing | Grants are version-specific and do not move automatically to a new release. | Provide Phaeno with the expected package and version. | | Access revoked | Phaeno ended the organization’s future access to that version. | Stop retrying and follow any governance instruction from Phaeno. | | Version quarantined | Future access is blocked while Phaeno reviews the release. | Do not use another link or another organization’s copy. Wait for Phaeno’s instruction. | | Package retired | The package is no longer available for new portal use. | Ask Phaeno whether an approved replacement exists. | | Download failed | The file or archive did not complete successfully. | Retry once. If it fails again, report the file name, package version, time, and safe error message. | | Checksum mismatch | The downloaded content is incomplete or changed. | Delete that copy, retry once, and contact Phaeno if the second checksum also fails. | | Wrong organization shown | The current session is scoped to a different membership. | Stop before opening or downloading data and contact Phaeno. | | Order action missing | Prospect organizations cannot place laboratory, reagent, or data-assembly orders. | Contact Phaeno if the business relationship should be reviewed. |

sections.heading: Report a problem safely
sections.text: Include the organization name, package name and version, file name when applicable, time of the event, and the portal’s safe error message. Do not attach downloaded data or send passwords, sign-in codes, invitation tokens, access tokens, browser storage, or another organization’s information.

guides.title: Trial Projects
guides.summary: Review and accept approved Trial scope, submit coded RNA, and download released results.

sections.heading: Your Trial Project
sections.text: A Trial Project is a no-charge, closed-ended PSeq evaluation of extracted RNA. Phaeno defines and approves its scope with you. It does not create a laboratory order, quote, invoice, or payment obligation. For Research Use Only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures. Do not enter protected health information (PHI), patient identifiers, medical record numbers, dates of birth, or direct personal identifiers. Use coded research references and keep any identity mapping outside the Portal.

sections.heading: Review and accept the scope
sections.text: Open Trial projects and select the Trial number. Confirm the selected organization and department. Active members can view approved Trials in their department; only an organization administrator can accept scope or submit samples. Department-administrator rights alone do not permit those actions. The workspace shows the objective, original sample allowance, submission opening and closing times, approved PSeq analyses, deliverables, acceptance criteria, material handling, and terms. Dates are displayed in your local time zone. Commercial and Scientific Operations approvals must come from two different authorized Phaeno people. Select Review and accept scope, read the complete approved scope in the dialog, and affirm the RUO/no-PHI terms. Acceptance applies to that scope revision. A later amendment requires new Phaeno approvals and your organization's acceptance again. Previous approved revisions remain available in the workspace.

sections.heading: Submit extracted RNA
sections.text: An organization administrator selects Submit samples while the approved submission window is open. In Submit extracted RNA samples, choose the extracted-RNA type and shipping destination for the batch. The form shows the required quantity unit and limits. Enter a unique coded reference, biological source, tube count, quantity, storage requirements, safety declaration, and the inputs required by the approved analyses for each sample. Concentration is required when an approved analysis requires it. Use Add another sample to prepare the roster, review each sample, and confirm RUO and no PHI. Submit the roster together to create one laboratory authorization and shipment for samples sharing that type and destination. Prepare separate submissions for different types or destinations. The submit button shows how many samples will be submitted. The original sample allowance is specific to this Trial. There is no automatic renewal or universal sample cap. If submission is unavailable, the workspace explains whether approval, acceptance, a hold, the time window, closure, or the allowance is responsible. Submitting creates the authorized laboratory work and a shipment awaiting Phaeno's return-kit preparation. Continue in Prepare and ship samples. Follow the approved packing and receiving instructions; submitting a record does not mean the material has been received. If Phaeno authorizes a replacement, choose the failed original sample in Approved replacement for. Each authorization allows one replacement and preserves the original history. A failed sample never grants an unapproved extra slot.

sections.heading: Follow progress and download results
sections.text: The workspace shows sample progress, customer-safe updates, and any schedule estimate. Trial estimates are not guaranteed turnaround times. A hold stops scientific progress and delivery while Phaeno resolves the issue. Partial results may become available before the entire Trial finishes. Their release does not start the complete-package retention period. When Phaeno releases all approved deliverables for the submitted samples, the Trial becomes Completed and the complete package receives its frozen retention policy. If the approved work cannot be completed, Phaeno records Closed incomplete with a reason. Use Download package for an available release archive, including its RUO manifest, or download an individual file. Download controls show progress and explain unavailable results. After complete release, earlier partial archives remain in history with a link to the complete package. Retention and receipt shows the package's manifest, frozen deadlines, download state, and retained lineage. The workspace refreshes after a transfer so availability and receipt information reflect the latest state. The initial file policy is 30 exact 24-hour days from complete release, with a warning five days before deletion if files remain undownloaded and a five-day grace period when required. Phaeno may configure organization overrides; the receipt shows your package's actual policy. A successful download by any authorized organization member satisfies that file for the organization. Failed or partial transfers do not count. Access may close earlier if the release is withdrawn or held. Deletion removes bytes; history and receipts remain and do not promise restoration.

sections.heading: Material, closure, and next steps
sections.text: Residual RNA normally remains for 30 days after terminal Trial closure, using the exact duration frozen in your scope. Phaeno records actual destruction, return, or exhaustion separately. Return is available only under arrangements approved before submission, including destination, handling, and shipping responsibility. Trial material is not reused for another purpose through this workflow. Trial completion does not convert your organization automatically. If Phaeno later converts it to Customer or Partner, approved Trial history remains under the same organization and department. Conversion does not extend download deadlines or permit new submissions to the old Trial. Further work requires a separate approved workflow. If a record changes while you are entering information, select Reload current Trial; keep my entries, review the updated scope and available choices, and resolve any entries that are no longer valid. A changed scope clears the acceptance confirmation so you must read and affirm the current terms before retrying. Your entries are kept if the reload fails. Editing, repeat actions, and dismissal are temporarily blocked while a submission or explicit reload finishes. Closing a form with changed entries asks whether to discard them. Contact Phaeno with the Trial number and the step that failed; do not send sample identity mappings or confidential scientific files in a support message.
